en: When Zen Master Shitō entered Pó’ān’s room, their milk and water met; they recognized the patch of wasteland left behind by their patriarch and, following the water-buffalo, took up the plow and the harrow.
Whether tilling or harvesting, they acted for the sake of all, pouring out their stores to provide great utility.
At the dharma assemblies in five locations, as the clouds gathered and bowls were spread, each person was enabled according to the power of their merit.

They were satisfied. As for those instances where laughter and jesting brought about restoration or turned the tilted and leaning back upright—these were all nothing other than the play of the *māyopama-samādhi* (the samādhi like an illusion).
When worldly conditions sought to discern him, he withdrew into the profound mystery. One does not know that on the fifteenth day of the third month, his final instructions were given;
yet, the single phrase of the public case, "If you obtain the root, do not worry about the branches," is already the definitive conclusion. O virtuous ones, realize this here!
[This] has been attained. Only now do we know that this old man’s profound silence is like the roar of thunder; there was originally one who does not die.
On the twentieth day of the ninth month in the sixth year of Chunyou, Cheng Gongsu, the "Man of Cangzhou," respectfully wrote this in his quarters at the Yutang (Jade Hall).
Kōfū Shōji was originally the place where Sekitō preached the Dharma. There was a custom there of solitary practitioners begging for alms in the villages during the day.
On the day the hearth was opened, Sekitō wished to gather clay figures to listen to the Dharma, yet even clay figures could not be found.
At that time, Kōgen Mukan—that is, Sōan Enshō—arrived together with me. When Sekitō ascended the hall, he looked at us with a smile and said, "A mere trifle of death."
"Fire atop the firewood: everyone, exert yourselves and try blowing on it! Amidst such solitude, his tone was like this.
Not long after, he moved to Fenglin. Regarding the "Picking up Antiquities," there are such remarks as, "Huanglong’s head and face are easy to see, but his heart and liver are difficult to perceive.
Yunchao praised him, Chijue recorded it in writing, and Zeweng also said, "I, the old monk, can do nothing but clear the way for him. Upon entering Yuan...
Wuguan said: "Though this is an old cart, I, this mountain monk, must push it sideways.

For twenty years thereafter, whenever the teachings were proclaimed across the mountains of the north and south—whether in places of plain reality or of perilous extremity—the leftward and rightward turns all constituted living mechanisms and active paths;
they are not easily exhausted by enumeration. I shall briefly record what I have personally heard and seen, lest it be thought that I am merely indulging in local bias.
It has not been forgotten. Please consult this record. Respectfully inscribed by Xinyue on the day of the commencement of the retreat during the Chunyou Dingwei year.

Recorded Sayings of the Jingci Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple, Lin’an Prefecture.
The Third Volume of the *Niangu Juan* (Anthology of Ancient Cases) from the *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings) of Lingyin Chan Temple,
Jingde, Lin’an Prefecture: A General Discourse on the Circumstances for Inviting [the Dharma Master].
Small Sermons and Dharma Discourses, Volume Four:
Verses and Hymns Praising the Buddhas and Patriarchs; Minor Buddhist Rituals.
Biographical Sketch, Memorial Inscription,
and Postscript to the Recorded Sayings of Venerable Shitō, Volume One:
The Recorded Sayings of Venerable Shitō upon his First Appointment at Gōkō Zen-in in the Prefecture of Pingjiang.
Compiled by his disciples Sitan and others at Zifu Chan Monastery in Longquan, Longxing Prefecture.
On the twenty-second day of the intercalary ninth month in the seventh year of the Jiading era, the Master entered the monastery.
Pointing to the three gates, he said: "This great gate of liberation has, from time immemorial, been entered and exited by all people alike.
Why is it that today it has instead become something extraordinary? After a long silence, he said: "I only fear that you all have forgotten."
In the Buddha Hall, the incense is burned and it is said: "Yunmen’s single blow; Gaofeng’s three prostrations. One house does not know the other;
each preserves its own boundaries."
Sitting in the abbot’s quarters, he said: "The abbot’s quarters of Gao Feng are empty both within and without. I cast my hook into the four seas, seeking only the fierce dragon.

Holding up a notice, he said: "This is the official warrant of a patch-robed monk; it stands out so suddenly that it is difficult to discern. Even with hands and eyes throughout one's entire body, one only attains half of it.
But tell me, where does the other half lie? Now, I ask the rector to provide a commentary on this."

Ascending the hall upon entering the monastery, he said: "Before the Buddhas appeared in the world, everyone’s nostrils reached up to the heavens. After they appeared in the world, there has been no news of their fragrance.
Today, I, Incense, have broken through my own skin; this gateway of mine is nothing other than this."
As long as every person throughout the entire world knows that the nostrils have always been upon the surface of the skin, do you all accept this announcement?
If you accept it, it is not necessarily a good cause that will bring about an evil result;

yet if you do not accept it, how can you avoid the fact that a cart cannot be pushed sideways, and that principle does not permit a crooked judgment? Among this assembly, is there anyone who can provide a hand to take up the task?
"Judi ma. If there is none, the new elder has lost his advantage. (The words of thanks are not recorded.
Again, it is cited that the Venerable Huayan Da Ci addressed the assembly, saying: "I, this old monk, cannot answer questions; I can only recognize the illness. At that time, a monk stepped forward.

Daci then returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master picked up the subject and said: "To employ the claws and fangs of the higher realm at the appropriate moment—Daci was certainly not lacking in this.
Yet, when examined closely, he merely provided a verbal answer; he did not recognize where the illness lay. Tell me, where does the error reside?
He let out a shout and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: When a monk approached, Luzu would simply turn his back to the wall. The Master commented:

"One day Luzu showed his compassion, yet he did not realize how much his own sinews and bones were laid bare. When a monk approached, Gaofeng would bow and inquire after him; if it was cold, he would say it was cold.
If it is hot, he says it is hot; he never dares to err by even a single hair’s breadth. Why? Because both are monastics.
On this auspicious occasion, as the Great Sage appears in the world, he transforms through silence and governs through non-action.

As we encounter this moment of auspicious celebration, ten thousand nations raise voices of joy; the Golden Wheel shall forever rule the three thousand worlds, and the Jade Leaves shall spread forth eternally.
A hundred million springs.

Entering the hall on the Winter Solstice: As the movement of the sun's shadow shifts, the longest day of the year arrives. Whether it be the Buddha-dharma or worldly dharmas, they follow one’s actions as one goes about one’s business.
Gao Feng further exhorts you all: first of all, do not sleep on cold ground.
Recorded Sayings of the Abbot of Fengqiao Puming Chan Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture, Compiled by His Dharma Heirs, Shitan, and Others.
On the twenty-first day of the first month in the eighth year of the Jiading era, the Master entered the monastery. Ascending the hall, he said: “Gautama held up [the flower]...”
Flowers. Bodhidharma faced the wall; writing characters in the dark, their patterns were already manifest. Kāśyapa broke into a smile; Shen Guang severed his arm to find peace of mind.
Their actions were similar; they came to be born into my house. From this point on, they have been transmitted through successive generations, like driving a wedge into empty space.
Throughout the vast forests of the world, everyone says, "I am the successor of the Yellow-Headed One and the Blue-Eyed One," each [claiming] for themselves.

To flaunt one's own abilities and present a chaotic display of ignorance is something you do not realize: carving sand can never produce the discourse of jade-carving, and weaving grass from the dead contradicts the intent of the Way-man.
Although Master Xun lacks any skillful means whatsoever, he would never harbor such a view.
Since one does not hold such a view, how ultimately does one establish [the teaching]? He struck his staff once and said:
"Habitually passing before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, hand in hand with a golden whip, celebrating peace. (The expression of gratitude is not recorded.
Furthermore, a monk asked Baizhang, "What is the extraordinary matter? Baizhang said, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak. The monk...
Baizhang bowed, and Baizhang struck him. The Master (Zhaozhou) remarked: "One question and one answer—set these aside for a moment.
Had it not been for Old Man Baizhang, my forehead would have nearly hit the ground. If someone were to ask me today, 'What is the extraordinary thing at New Fengqiao?
I would simply say to them: 'On a sunny spring day, the yellow oriole sings.'"
The Buddha ascends the hall for the occasion of his *parinirvāṇa*. On the full moon of the second month of spring, Gautama enters *nirvāṇa*;

Māra dances with both hands, while Kāśyapa knits his two brows. Looking at this from a cool distance, it is all but the idle moonlight that shines upon Chang’an night after night. (He lets out a shout.)
Ascending the hall, he said: "The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha does not pass through fire; the clay Buddha does not pass through water.
But tell me, where exactly does the true Buddha reside? One only knows that affairs pass before one’s eyes, yet fails to realize that old age creeps upon one from above."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "One is direct; two is circuitous. If a patch-robed monk understands this, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences.
With eyes idly cast before the courtyard, spring has ended yet flowers still remain. It was not fitting for the Old Barbarian to cross the shifting sands."
The Hall Discourse for the Buddha-Bathing Ceremony: In the past, when Yaoshan and Nun Zun were bathing the Buddha in the hall, Yaoshan asked Zun, "You can bathe only this one;
but you cannot bathe that one. Zun replied, "Bring me that one and I will bathe it. Yaoshan then desisted.
Great assembly, the exchange between Yaoshan and Nun Zun—this coming and going—is very much like a laborious effort.
Yet there is no merit. Even so, although it is thus, Yaoshan has ceased. How many people understand this as "ceasing"? But do not understand it as ceasing.
Ultimately, how will you understand it? Descend from the seat; let us go together to the hall, and I shall explain it through for you all.
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: Mañjuśrī instructed Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs, saying, "Bring back whatever is medicine.
Sudhana searched everywhere; there was nothing that was not medicine. He returned and reported, "There is nothing that is not medicine. Mañjuśrī said, "Then bring back whatever is medicine.
Sudhana then picked up a single blade of grass and handed it to Mañjuśrī. Mañjuśrī took it up and showed it to him.
The assembly said, "This medicine can kill people, and it can also bring people back to life. The Master picked up the point and said, "Śāriputra gathered it;
Mañjuśrī used it. To kill or to bring to life, one must wield it according to the immediate occasion. You must look directly into the palace of the sea dragon;
do not look at the waves surging before your eyes."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Zhimen, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?

Zhimen said, "The lotus flower. [The monk asked,] "What is it like after it has emerged from the water? Zhimen said, "The lotus leaf. The Master commented: "Lotus flower, lotus leaf—the meaning lies before words."
The wondrous secret instructions of the immortals are not transmitted even between father and son.
Entering the hall: The essence of the Great Way is vast; it is neither easy nor difficult. Measuring the head to buy a hat—this land is the Western Heaven.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old case: "In the past, there was a scholar who wrote a 'Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts. One day, a ghost manifested its form and said, 'You say there are no ghosts;
what about me? The scholar was speechless. Later, the Fifth Patriarch said, 'At that time, he should have simply raised his hand and made the beak of a magpie, saying, "Gu-gua-gu.
The Master offered this verse: The Fifth Patriarch’s magpie cries out; He seizes the moment and raises it directly.
Seeking ant tracks across a mountain—how many can truly know?
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: "In the autumn of the eighth month, where is there heat? Even the monk Du has not yet glimpsed it.
At the dead of night, hearing with the eyes; how could one pick out the moon in the heavens?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Teachings say: 'To know thus, to see thus, and to believe and understand thus'—a person who has already paid their debt does not owe further credit.
Here at Fengqiao, the purchase and sale are already finalized; whether the price is fair or not is yet to be seen."

Opening the furnace, he ascended the hall. He cited the story of Danxia passing through a monastery during a freezing cold spell. Thereupon, inside the hall, he took a wooden Buddha and burned it toward the fire.
The monastery director happened to see this and rebuked him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha? Danxia prodded the fire with his staff and said, "I am burning for the sake of the *śarīra*.
The director said, "A wooden Buddha—how could it have *śarīra*? Danxia replied, "If there were none," [he would not have burned it].
"Śāriputra, please burn two more statues. Afterward, the head of the monastery’s eyebrows and beard fell out. The Master commented:
"When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, the man was poor and his wisdom short; when the head of the monastery’s eyebrows and beard fell out, the colors ran to the clumsy householder.
There is yet another final stroke left for all of you to contemplate at the side of the brazier."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Master Foyan, who said: "Day by day, moment by moment, the old man of Longmen knows it in his own heart. The Master commented:
"Big and small, the Old Man of Longmen has not yet emerged from the realm of shadows. Fengqiao says: 'Day by day, moment by moment;
the mouth is like the nose, the eyes are like the eyebrows. Twisting hemp rope with the left hand to bind the ghost-child, he turns around and shoots the essential target with a weed-arrow.'"
Mi. Tuo! On this New Year’s Day, ascending the hall:
the Buddha-dharma of the new year is fully manifest. Brightness departs and darkness arrives; three heads and two faces.
Even a sharp-witted patch-robed monk is still separated by a single thread. To ask further, "How about this?"—it is like pulling an arrow from behind one's head.

Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: pointing to heaven, pointing to earth—this is but the play of a small child; there is nothing earnest about it. Pouring a ladle of foul water. Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat:
during the ninety-day *an-guo* (summer retreat), the eyebrows are knotted together. When one person gives rise to the true and returns to the source, the voids of the ten directions shatter asunder.
But tell me, after they have shattered, what then? A rat gnawing iron.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is Zhaozhou? Zhaozhou replied, “The east gate, the south gate, the west gate, the north gate.
The Master commented: “Do you all understand? The goods are at their set price; the coins are full-value.”

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The true mechanism of the Buddhas and Patriarchs has never been subject to measurement. Like hooks and locks in a continuous chain, it cannot be extracted even with a blade.
Shitian has a way of explaining it, yet perhaps none of you fully comprehend it: *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*, the most profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the saying of the Patriarch: "The mind turns with the myriad objects; where it turns, it is truly profound. Following the flow, one recognizes one's nature;
there is neither joy nor sorrow. The Master commented: "The Patriarch spoke thus, both completing all people and ruining all people.
Tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie? Let those with eyes discern it!"
Ascending the hall: “In Pūrvavideha to the east and Aparagoyānī to the west, in the clear, pure waters, the swimming fish are lost in their own confusion.
Ascending the hall: [The Master] cites the verse of the Fifth Patriarch: “The golden chrysanthemums bloom in the courtyard as the old roots sprout anew;

The returning geese are heard with a fresh cry or two. Last night, the Seven Peaks stirred my old passion; A thousand thoughts and ten thousand reflections reached the break of dawn. The Master comments: “The Fifth...”
The Patriarch’s words were clear as day; those who understood his heart were few. At Fengqiao Bridge, it is not so:

golden chrysanthemums bloom in the courtyard from their old roots, and the new news of returning geese sounds once or twice. Still grasping his golden whip, he asks the traveler returning home: "In the deep night, who will walk with me along the Imperial Street?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The sick from hunger are parched; the hungry from sickness are clamoring. Before the donkey’s business has departed, the horse’s business arrives.
At such a time as this, tell me: is there still any meaning of the Patriarchs? Beneath the green pines by the ancient stream, a long-lasting茯苓 (fuling) fungus grows for a thousand years."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Going east is also the Head Seat; going west is also the Head Seat. Drawing water and setting fire, reading the wind and setting the rudder;
appearing in seven ways and disappearing in eight. Elegant and refined, yet how many times have black winds overturned the great ocean?
Yet when has the fishing boat ever been capsized?"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Ciming, "When one travels on pilgrimage and encounters no one, what then?

Ciming replied, "A fishing line twisting in the water. The Master offered this verse: Old and decrepit Ciming points out the way for the lost; The fishing line twisting in the water stirs the myriad functions.
At that time, people were so greedy to gaze at the white reeds that they did not see the sandpipers flying across the shore.
On the eighth day of the twelfth month, Śākyamuni ascended the hall; suddenly beholding the morning star, his eye-sight was lost—like a defeated general.
No need to laboriously bring it forth. You people, with these two eyes of yours—seeing the sun by day and seeing the stars by night—do not travel the paths beneath the mountains;
there, the cries of monkeys are sounds that break one's heart.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The staff and the shout are applied together; like thunder crashing and lightning flashing. Within the matter of the Original Inquiry, there is no connection at all.
That there is no connection has its reason: last night at the third watch, the ox was lost. He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, Luyuan addressed the assembly, saying: "The direct meaning of the West—how difficult it is to speak of!
Is there no one who can say it? Come forward and speak! At that time, a monk stepped forth. Luyuan said, "What kind of season is this now?
Why have you put your head out? The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Luyuan’s words conceal swords and halberds; this monk releases folly from within his guile."
"Han! This is the very intent of the one who came from the West.
Scratching my forehead, I gaze toward Fusang. Entering the hall, he said: "Cast away one; pick up seven. The great road that penetrates heaven—ten thousand layers of iron walls.

The heart, liver, and five viscera of Fengqiao Bridge are all at once laid bare. This stinking bone is cast with full confidence. Of the hundreds of thousands of kinds of spiritual powers, they require nothing more than this."
He said, "There is no need to speak of it.

He ascended the hall and said: "The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different. Dragging along from Silla to fight for forehead-to-forehead dominance with Campā—this lame-legged master still falls into the secondary rank.
East, west, south, north—from where have they come? It is well said: 'From the very beginning...'"
Teaching the Ducks to Listen to Thunder. Entering the Hall:
"If you recognize your own mind, mountains and peaks sink away. Grasping gold turns it into earth; grasping earth turns it into gold. Behind the feet, before the feet."
Behold the completed practice and goods; before the peak of Shaoshi, the points of intersection do not pass one another.
On the Winter Solstice, he ascends the hall: "To understand speech is not a matter of the tongue; to be able to speak is not the sound itself.
He brings forth a fresh, living phrase: after winter, the first yang arises.
Ascending the hall: A single word exhausts the path; yet it becomes two separate pieces. Beating the drum and ascending the hall: the son inherits the father’s legacy. Ascending the hall:
leaving one grove and entering another grove—without the eye for traveling the pilgrimage routes, it is difficult to penetrate the mind of the Patriarch.
The earth extends beyond the eight frontiers; the heavens have no four walls. I recall a time when Nanquan lived in a mountain hut many years ago;
there was a certain keen-witted practitioner whose news has remained utterly silent until this very day.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The autumn wind is high; the autumn leaves fall. Monks run about wildly to the ends of the earth and the corners of the sea.
He took up his staff and struck it once, saying: "Even though this is so, it does not go beyond this very thing. He then leaned the staff against the wall and said: "I let this one move pass."

Ascending the hall, he said: "When the eyes encounter things, one does not recognize the Way; when the feet move, how can one know the steps? To empty one's belly and pour out one's heart would only result in a formal proclamation.
You who wear this stone field upon your heads—how could you dare to err by even a hair’s breadth? Yet I recall Old Teacher Wang: he did not beat this broken drum."
When the Elder of Lingyin arrived, he ascended the hall and spoke. He cited the case of Layman Luoshan visiting Elder Tan.
When Tan reached the midpoint of the road, he brewed tea to welcome him and personally served the tea. As Luoshan took the cup, Tan asked, "How is this tea?
Luoshan took a sip and spat it out. Tan laughed heartily. The Master commented: "Elder Tan invited a thief to ruin his house; Luoshan simply..."
A nest of bandits! Even if you were to investigate and verify this, you could not avoid the clashing of skulls. But tell me:
when Lingyin meets Fengqiao today, what will happen? Both will know shame.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Bodhidharma did not understand Chan; Confucius did not know how to read. First, do not bring anything forward; what you bring forward will not be like it.
Do you all wish to understand? (He struck his staff once and said: To emerge from the head is to die."
Ascending the hall, he raised up the example of Master Panshan, who said: "Like the earth supporting a mountain, it does not know the mountain's towering loftiness;
like a stone containing jade, it does not know the jade's flawlessness. He struck the meditation staff once and said: "What a pity for Old Panshan!
He shaved his head and donned the kashaya."

Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: This is not a mundane worldly dharma, nor is it the intent of the Western Patriarchs. As the movements of the sun’s shadow shift, the days grow longer as we reach the southern solstice.
The stone man at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou does not speak of how time is being wasted in vain.
Ascending the hall: One does not become one; two do not become two. Drinking water, it becomes water; striking the bone, the marrow comes forth.
The eyes have pupils; when color appears, they are raised up.
Ascending the hall: No mind and no dharma; neither dharma nor mind. Great merit goes unrewarded; the thatched gate is overgrown with weeds. Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival:
Throughout one’s entire being there is nowhere to seek; the whole world has never been hidden. Closing one's eyes, one sits through the Mid-Autumn moon. Yet...
The laughing moon has no light.
Entering the hall, he said: "Last night I drew my bow and shot through the void; it fell scattered in pieces, beyond all gathering up.
Is there anyone among you who can gather it up? Even if you were able to gather it up, you would still not escape the heavy staff of Shitien."
"It is not permitted. Why? One may forgive the killing of a person, but such lack of propriety is difficult to tolerate.
He ascended the hall and said: "Since the time of the Patriarchs, everyone has misunderstood. It is indeed a mistake; it is a mistake.
At Shitian, today I shall treat this like a dead horse with medicine. He then took up his staff, struck once, and said: "In what direction does this mistake go? Liang.
Jiuyun said: "Guests at Longmen are few; people in the bustling market are many. He ascended the hall.
Waving his hand across the river, he diagnosed the situation according to the occasion. One who crosses by running sideways suffers from a terminal illness.
The road lies right before the Maple Forest Gate; it has never been separated from the river. Let the monks come and go as they please; he has never even waved his hand. Why is this?

The *kāṣāya* robes are shared across shoulders. On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascends the hall: "Every person on this great earth possesses the eye; the morning star shines its brilliance night after night.
Gautama failed to seize the opportunity and lost a pair of eyebrows. How could the descendants of later generations know? Once a year, they bring forth a jumble of needles and hammers."

The Head Administrative Officer ascends the hall. Whether the monastery is large or small, and whether the assembly is numerous or few, there is this broken-legged cauldron that requires someone to lift it up and carry it down—neither falling into the realm of worldly achievement nor colliding with social conventions. It is like pursuing the wind for a thousand miles to observe a fine horse.
The Discourse Record of the Chan Master of Taiping Xingguo Chan Monastery in Jiankang Prefecture,
compiled by his dharma heirs, including the masters Liaojue and Shitan, et al.
The Master entered the monastery on the second day of the fourth month in the sixteenth year of the Jiading era.
Pointing to the three gates, he said: "Having penetrated the secure barrier, one strides alone across the horizontal and vertical. Wherever one’s feet reach is one’s livelihood;
who says there is no path on this mountain? Sitting upon the abbot’s seat, he said: "The forges of Miam, Ying’an, and Yuanwu have once been opened here. Though it is an old place..."
"The carriage. The mountain monk, however, wishes to push it sideways. Is there anyone who does not feel a sense of dissatisfaction? He lets out a shout.
Entering the hall, he holds up the incense and says: "This first offering of incense is respectfully for..."
He offered prayers for the supreme sovereign at the Northern Gate, wishing for the holy longevity of the Southern Mountain. He then adjusted his robes and took his seat.

A monk asked, "The Buddhas hand over the transmission to one another, and the Patriarchs pass it down from one to the next. But when neither Buddha nor Patriarch had yet arisen, how did they communicate this?
The Master replied, "There is no need to hang up the stone mirror; when dawn breaks, all is naturally clear. The monk said, "If that is so, then the Eye of the True Dharma..."

[The Master] sent it out for circulation in the treasury. The monk replied, "This too is like using a ladle to divine by listening to empty sounds. The monk said, "As soon as the Wheel of Dharma is turned, ordinary beings and sages intermingle.
At such a time, how do you offer blessings to the Emperor? [The Master] replied, "The myriad phenomena all shout 'Long Live! in unison.

The monk said, "I have already received your instruction regarding the blessing of the Emperor; as for the matter of the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, what is it like? [The Master] replied:
[The Master] said, "Six ears do not share a secret. The monk said, "I thank the Master for his response," and then prostrated.
The Master then said, "Buddha to Buddha, hand to hand; Patriarch to Patriarch, transmitted from one to another.
The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye flows through the ages, not leaking a single drop, never shifting by a hair’s breadth. Today it rests entirely in the hands of Xiangshan. It has always been thus."
"Go! The entire earth is a desolate peak. Coming along in this manner, countless people have passed through empty space by seizing upon nothingness.
Apart from these two paths, is there anyone who can discern the hidden whereabouts of New Jiangshan?

After a long silence, he said: "If it were not for the hand of Monk You, one would merely be speaking of painted colors. (The expression of thanks is not recorded. He then raised the case of Master Baogong, who sent someone to deliver a message.
Dashi Daoshi said, "Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings? Why do you simply gaze at the clouds and the Milky Way?
Dashi Daoshi replied, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where are there any sentient beings to be saved? The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "How great and how small was Dashi Daoshi! He could not hold his ground; he was lightly squeezed by Master Baoguang."
Thereupon, he shifted his entire body and moved away. Shituan took his leave of the maple grove and ascended Mount Jiang.
He saw no Buddhas to be swallowed, nor did he see any sentient beings to be saved. But tell me, how ultimately does he act for the sake of others? After a long silence, he said:
"Transversely grasping the Mohe sword, he maintains the full authority of the True Command; throughout the realm of Great Peace, he slays the dull and the stubborn."
Ascending the hall: Having newly settled at Mount Zhong, all matters are as they should be; there is nothing that is not acceptable, whether turned to the left or the right.
That small point where it does not accord with the universal way—presumably you all do not yet know it. But tell me, where is this point at Mount Zhong that does not accord with the universal way?
Look for it five days from now.

"Please, Head Seat, hang the plaque and ascend the hall. To cite the ancients and the present, to mix mud with water, and to speak of mind and nature, is like painting a tiger and ending up with a wildcat.
Therefore it is said: 'A thousand people pushing against the gate are not as good as one person pulling the bolt. One person pulling the bolt—"
"Thousands and tens of thousands have attained the ground of doubtless peace and bliss. Now tell me: who is it that breaks through the barrier?
[The Master] descends from his seat and, together with the administrative officers, the head monks, and the assembly, makes an exhortation to the Venerable Qīngzhēn.
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is jade within the stone, but no oil in the sand. Deshan and Linji have not yet emerged from the common stream.
I recall instead the son of Hanshan, as he stands at an ancient ferry crossing."
Xie [the Abbot] ascends the hall to the head seat. He cites Master Yunmen’s address to the assembly:
“On level ground there are countless dead people; he who penetrates the thorn-brake is a true adept.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, “If that is so, then the first seat in the hall must have some excellence. Yunmen said, “Suru suru. The Master comments: “Yunmen’s eye—”
His presence filled the four seas and his spirit was like that of a sovereign; yet, when this monk gave him a light squeeze, he found no way to remain hidden.
If it had been Jiangshan, he would have waited for him to say, "In that case, the first seat in the hall has something superior."
He simply said to him: "Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish; a patch-robed monk is difficult to deceive.
He ascended the hall and said: "In this way, in this way—the meaning yields a bountiful year. Not in this way, not in this way—frugality gives rise to unfiliality."
A man of clear vision has no fixed abode; he turns water into ice and treats the non-existent as existent. A jade palace and a crystal tower are but a single blade of grass—how extraordinary!
Today at Jiangshan, for no reason at all, I act as a guarantor for people on level ground.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Dharma is thus; how can one provide guidance? The ancient Buddhas and the pillar interpenetrate day and night.
Although Jiangshan speaks thus, there were those in the West who could not bear it."
Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat. On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, the retreat is closed; empty space is scorched by fire.
This land and the Western Heaven share the same path, yet not the same tracks. Since they share the same path, why do they not share the same tracks? A radish from Zhenzhou, iron from Bingzhou.
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth: Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. Stone fields have no remaining words. The ghost-gate is shattered;
at the third watch, the sun stands at noon. Even the clear-eyed monk is lost on the path.
Ascending the hall, he said: "This is a ready-made case; it cannot be resolved by mere intellectual analysis. To hear its fame for a thousand years is not as good as seeing it once in person.
But tell me, after seeing it in person, what is there to do? One has a mouth only fit for eating rice."
Ascending the hall: In the midst of deep mountains and rocky cliffs, in a remote place utterly devoid of people, this matter is clear and manifest in its entirety.
To attempt to grasp it is to deviate; not to attempt it is to fall into error. Zhaozhou personally saw Nanquan;
Baizhang once studied under Mazu.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Dongshan, “When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them? Dongshan said, “Avoid them where there is no cold and no heat.
The monk asked, “What is the place where there is no cold and no heat? Dongshan said, “When it is cold, let the cold kill you; when it is hot, let the heat kill you.
The Master commented: “The ground is stable and secure; the pivot is clear and resonant. To recognize this—”
One attains a place where neither cold nor heat exists; let cold and heat assail as they may. Here, the path is the same, yet the ways differ.
On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and cited Chan Master Cheng of Changsha.

One evening, while he and Master Yangshan were admiring the moon, Yangshan said, "Everyone possesses this very thing, yet it simply cannot be used. Changsha said, "Precisely so; I shall borrow it from you."
Yangshan said, "How do you use it? Changsha then gave him a kick and knocked him down.
As Yangshan rose up, he said, "You are truly like a great tiger. The Master commented: "Changsha’s insight was intimate, yet his application was coarse;
Yangshan called out with his mouth but was cunning in his belly. Truly, what a fine tiger! A pity it is already gone."
[The Master] said, "It wounds my teeth and claws.
He ascended the hall and raised the following case: Upāsaka Xianying went to visit Ciming. Ciming asked, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Jinluan.
[Ciming asked], "Where were you during the summer retreat? "Jinluan. [Ciming asked], "Where were you last summer? "Jinluan. [Ciming asked], "Where were you the summer before that? "Jinluan."
Luan asked, "Where was Xia previously? Why did you not understand his words? Ming said, "I am also unable to examine you;
I shall have a servant from the storehouse examine you. For now, let me serve you a cup of tea to moisten your parched lips.
The Master commented: "A fired brick strikes the frozen ground to its very core; red-eyed, one bumps into a firebrand. The General has only obtained the auspiciousness."
The sound is here. Why must one seek the honor of being enfeoffed as a Marquis of Ten Thousand Households?
Entering the hall: seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing; walking, standing, sitting, and reclining—before you even raise a single eyebrow, you have already missed it.
Barefoot, singing a mountain song, there is no one on the road to join him.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "From the Buddhas and Patriarchs of old down to all the elder monks of the world—*thumping his staff once*—they all seek their lives here.
*Thumping it once more*, he said: 'A general amnesty is granted; all are released.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Right here! Right here! A dull bird does not leave its nest; a fine steed travels ten thousand miles.
This old fellow Deshan has, for thirty years, never once struck one who is truly liberated. Is there anyone among the disciples of Jiangshan who is liberated?
They too must carry tea and sweep the floor."
Ascending the hall: Body and mind are as one; there is nothing beyond the body. Though Chang’an is pleasant, it is not a place for long residence. Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival:
When I see the Buddha of Lamp-Light, a single film obscures the eye. The auspicious radiance of the original light is like this—empty flowers falling in confusion.
Mountains are mountains; waters are waters. For the patch-robed monk, what need is there for inscriptions or records to be seen by the eyes or heard by the ears? *Ei!*
"Xuan Sha has reached the bottom. Xuan Sha has reached the bottom. He ascended the hall and said:
"Zen is not a matter of conceptual thought; the Way is beyond all achievement. Under the blue sky and bright sun, there are those who lose their way—can there be anyone who does not lose their way?
Having secured Annam, one still worries about the north of the Great Wall."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Lingyun attained enlightenment upon seeing peach blossoms—this is like a snake burrowing into a mouse hole. Guishan said: 'Those who enter through conditions shall never again fall back.
To grieve for others' grief as one's own; Xuansha said: 'I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate. To rejoice in others' joy as one's own.
If one is a person who climbs the cassia tree in the Broad Cold Palace, they carry both the branches and the leaves."
The leaves and roots are pulled up by the roots.
Entering the hall: "Two days of sun, three days of rain; for the patch-robed monks, there is not a single spot where their skin and grass robes can be dried. Jiangshan beats the weeds."
As long as there is a startled snake, even flawless white jade will have its flaws.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "Those whose ground is stable and secure cannot be pierced by a needle; those who sport with supernatural powers act with sovereign ease in every direction."
If you arrive here at Mount Jiangshan, you cannot help but be set down all at once. Gold is never sold mixed with sand.

[Addressing] Xie Houtang, the Secretary, as he ascends the hall: Where words and explanations fail to reach, and before the traces of literary expression have arisen—even lightning and sparks are still too slow.
If you can directly take up this burden across your body, a single strand of lotus fiber will move the five Sumeru mountains.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When the heavy barrier is firmly closed, the lives of all of you are in the hands of this mountain monk.
When a single thread is let loose, the life of this mountain monk is in your hands. Now, I neither close it firmly nor let it loose.
This mountain monk is you; you are this mountain monk. Thirty years from now, do not say that Jiangshan has merely mixed mud."
Mixing the water.
On the occasion of the commencement of the retreat, I ascend the hall: within the Great Perfect Enlightenment, there is no rope with which to bind oneself.

For the sake of this monastery, where ordinary and holy beings intermingle, body and mind dwell in peace. Changing the water to nourish the fish, the wisdom of equality falls into the secondary; do not let it be in vain.
Two eyebrows. Ninety days from this very day.
Entering the hall: as clear as the sun, as black as lacquer. One dog barks at the void; a thousand monkeys gnaw at the jewel. This mountain monk has a mouth.
Having hung it upon the wall for a long time, I trouble my staff to deliver a message to you all. (He strikes the staff once.
"The patch-robed monks of this eastern land are coarse of heart; the waxen figures of the Western Heavens shed tears."

Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth: Today is the Double Fifth Festival. Mount Zhong is stubbornly loquacious. Since there is no White泽 (Bai Ze) diagram in the house, demons and monsters naturally vanish.
Vanish! Vanish! When walking at night, one may freely covet the bright moon.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Since the time of the Patriarchs, no one has been able to do anything about it. Deshan and Linji have needlessly raised the banner of war.
He struck his knee once and said: "When water reaches the vast ocean, it is no longer called a wave."

Ascending the hall: If you have not yet crossed the pass of Jiangshan, you must cross the pass of Jiangshan. Once you have crossed the pass of Jiangshan, you cannot be called back and cannot be confined.
A great wave surges upon level ground; white rain falls from the blue sky. The stony field smiles broadly.
I did not dare to grant my consent lightly. Why? Because if one shoots at a tiger without being true to it, one merely exhausts oneself until the feathers of the arrow are lost.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "Level as a mirror, yet mired like mud. To be deluded is to be deluded regarding awakening; to awaken is to awaken regarding delusion.
Where the power of Yu does not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west."

Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Baling, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? Baling said, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree;
when the duck is cold, it enters the water. The Master commented: "Although Baling did not fail to respond to the immediate impulse of the questioner, he was still stuck at two heads and three horns.
If someone were to ask me, Jiangshan, whether the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings are the same or different, I would simply say to him:"
The Way: south of the Yangtze it becomes a mandarin orange; north of the Yangtze it becomes a *zhǐ* tree. Now tell me, is there any distinction of superiority or inferiority?
Let those with eyes discern this.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "Striking the void produces sound; hitting wood makes no noise. If you still do not understand—"
The staff of Mount Jiangshan has now entered the Land of Pure Wonder and once again expounds the Dharma-gate of liberation.
He then struck it once and descended from the seat.
Entering the hall, he said: "By brushing away dust one sees the Buddha, yet the Buddha is also dust. If you can find rest right here, then..."
Without looking up in aspiration, cut off your own self from below; throughout the twelve hours of the day, what further matter could there be?
Nevertheless, even so, take care, lest you run into Master Dushun.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Way is not outside of things; that which is outside of things is not the Way. At Jiangshan, every day I receive guests in the abbot’s quarters and practice seated meditation in the monks’ hall.
Now tell me: is this the Way, or is it things? If you can discern this, I shall give you a pair of trousers."
The Recorded Sayings of Jingci Baoen Guangxiao Chan Temple in Lin’an Prefecture, compiled by the Dharma-heirs Liaojue, Sitan, and others, included in the Three Gates.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "The Peak of Wisdom-Sun is high; the gate and courtyard stand like a sheer cliff. Letting down a single thread, from this..."
Entering the inner chamber, the Abbot said: "First, the direct path; second, the circumstantial approach. To capture tigers and rhinoceroses, one must distinguish dragons from snakes.
The white jade is flawless, yet it possesses a flaw."
He held up the imperial decree and said, "The edict has descended from the Ninefold Palace; the entire nation knows it. Yet as for this one phrase that strikes at the head, none of you understand it.
Now, does the new Elder understand? After a long silence, he said: 'It would be better to cut out one's tongue than to violate the imperial taboo.'"

Ascending the seat, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The path beyond the ordinary is not so even for the thousand sages. Before one's eyes there is no other grass; beneath one's feet lies the blue sky.
He then strode up to the seat, took up the incense, and said:

"I respectfully offer this incense to extend the holy longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! I pray that the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas shall protect..."
May Your Majesty’s life be boundless; for ten million years and more, may it remain as indestructible as a vajra.
This single offering of incense is respectfully presented to extend blessings to the Empress Dowager.

To His Sacred Majesty: We humbly pray that you may enjoy great peace and glory, facing eternal and boundless inquiries for ten thousand and ten million years, and alone beholding the longevity of those who possess the Way.
This single incense offering is respectfully presented for the Junior Tutor, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Grand Chancellor, Duke of the State, and Grand Councilor, the Minister.

To the Chancellor of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Acting Chancellor of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Vice Minister of the Pacification Commission, the Commissioner for Transport, the Palace Secretary, and all the civil and military officials of the court: may you enjoy increased longevity and prosperity.
We humbly pray that you, both in arms and in letters, remain ever loyal and filial, forever serving as pillars of the Imperial Court and remaining eternally...
This single offering of incense is for the Holy Sovereign’s ministers and limbs: it is offered to the late Great Monk Pò’ān, who formerly resided at Fèngshān Zīfú in Ānjì Prefecture.
Rather than seeking to repay his virtue or requite his kindness, I have simply decided to treat him with a thorough and blunt disregard.

Thereupon, the Master respectfully donned his robes and took his seat. At that time, a monk stepped forward and asked, "Beneath Mount Nanping and before Huiri Peak, the field for selecting buddhas has opened;
we pray that the Master will offer prayers for the Emperor. He replied, "The heavens are high and the myriad creatures are upright; the seas are vast and the hundred rivers flow toward them."

The monk said, “I have already received your instruction regarding the blessing of the Emperor. But as for this field where Buddhas are selected, is there anyone who has attained the ‘passing of the examination’ through the emptiness of mind?
The Master replied, “In every person, the constant light is ever-present; each and every one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
The monk asked, “If, among them, there were suddenly someone who did not enter this protective community, would you, O Monk, still accept him? The Master replied, “Thirty.”
[The Master] held up his staff and said, "Let us go; we shall discuss this another time. A monk asked, "Why not grant me the transmission face-to-face?

He replied, "You ignorant fellow who cannot even recognize pain or itch! The monk then bowed. The Master then said: "Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are the Dharma, yet the Dharma is apart from seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing.
Before entering the gate of Nanping, the lake and sky were vast and shimmering, and fish and birds forgot their artifice. Once having entered the gate of Nanping, the pavilions..."
The pavilion is towering and majestic; its gold and green dazzle the eyes. Those sitting see those standing, and those standing see those sitting.
The wondrous, perfect, and penetrating realization lies precisely at this moment. This is how one can repay the unrequitable debt of gratitude and assist in the transformation of non-action.
If it be otherwise, the new Elder will suffer repeated losses. (The words of thanks are not recorded. He further cited Emperor Taizong, who—due to...
A monk was presented for an audience with the Emperor. The Emperor asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "From Wo-yun Hermitage on Mount Lu.
The Taizong Emperor said, "In the depths of the Cloud-Residing [Wo-yun] mists, one does not face the court; why then have you come here? The monk was speechless. Xuedou spoke on his behalf:
"It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation. The Master (Zhaozhou) commented: "The Great Man Taizong possessed great vision; this monk possessed great wisdom and attained great function."
Although Xuedou did not fail to respond to the immediate occasion, he could not avoid the situation where "the shrimp leaps but cannot get out.
Had it been the new Elder, at that time he would have simply replied: "Today, a small emergence meets a great encounter. Now tell me: does this accord with the Sage’s intention?
After a long silence, he said: "Habitually passing before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, hand in golden whip, celebrating the Great Peace."
The Master ascends the hall to thank the attendants: "A multitude of streams form the sea; a multitude of hairs form a ball. Upon one stage, a magnificent falcon—refined and elegant.
In the stony fields there is not a single thing; sitting on the ground, he gazes at Yangzhou."
Ascending the hall: Having just arrived at Shitien, affairs are in a state of bustle; one grasps the nostrils but loses the eyes.
As for the two words "Buddha-dharma," I do not fear they will rot away. For now, listen as those from all quarters practice blows and shouts.
The posthumous writings of Master Zhe arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "A teacher of fifteen hundred people does not consider our school to be in a state of profound stillness.

Five Peaks kicks over the mountain, waves overturning the void; the great earth, mountains, and rivers all lose their luster. The essence of the golden wind is revealed; leaves fall and return to the root.
It is only fit for sorrow, not fit for lingering on."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you do not seal the Vairocana mudrā, how can you propagate the mind of the ancient Buddha? The bright moon shines upon the secluded valley;
the cold waves assist the night mortar. The Master added: "In the mountains of Mount Fahu, Master Jue, my uncle, carries his single wooden board in vain all the way until this very day."
This was not brought forth by Shitian; it nearly sinks into oblivion as it is. How many, upon hearing the string, can truly appreciate the music?
On the occasion of the first anniversary of Emperor Ningzong’s passing, he ascended the hall and said: "The transformations of the Perfect Man are subtle and difficult to name.

His coming and going do not rely on images; his movement and stillness do not rely on form. The thoroughfare is naturally vast and remote; where is there that does not honor him? Furthermore, there is not a single dharma."
One may act according to one's own nature; tread directly upon the crown of Vairocana’s head.
Elder of Jiangshan arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "Upon Duren Peak, before Huiri Peak, the clouds and moon are the same, yet the streams and mountains differ.
The Eye of the True Dharma breaks the sand bowl. I urge you to drink one more cup of wine as you depart westward beyond the Yang Pass."
No old acquaintances.
Ascending the hall: The wind whistles, the rain whistles; not a hair’s breadth of movement, one strides level-footed across the crimson heavens. To go thus—straightaway.
Even the earth beneath the gates of Nanshan is difficult to digest.
Entering the hall, he said: "Upon this lump of red flesh, it stands like a wall ten thousand fathoms high. Linji and Deshan used the heterodox to strike the orthodox;
their interlocking patterns and crisscrossing nodes wrap around in hundreds of layers and thousands of folds. In a casual toss of a single hook, the dragon of the azure abyss is startled awake."
Ascending the hall: Not a single thread of silk hangs, yet the bare flesh remains. Yellow-headed and blue-eyed, they have no door through which to cry out their grievances.
I walk amidst the wild weeds; you, again, enter the deep village.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The eternal void of ten thousand ages; the wind and moon of a single day. Since the time of the Patriarchs, this has been spoken of as two separate pieces.
Shitian speaks with such clarity: 'An eighty-year-old old man chewing raw iron.'"

Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year: The sun and moon are as they have always been; the mountains and rivers remain as before. The Buddha-dharma of the New Year is, quite simply, a battle of spears and shields.
(He strikes the meditation staff once. When water reaches the vast ocean, it is no longer called "waves."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The entire earth is not oneself—this is a thicket of thorns reaching to the heavens.
The entire earth is entirely oneself—this is dust filling one's eyes. Transverse and vertical, clenching and releasing; if you wish to meet the Southern Mountain, bring me back my first tally!"
Xie Zhushan ascends the hall: "Bright as the sun; black as lacquer. The great road that penetrates heaven; ten thousand layers of iron walls.
The mouth of Nanshan is like a blood-basin—how would anyone dare recklessly transmit news? Why? Because one stands before those with clear eyes."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Supreme Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination.

Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars, grasses, trees, forests, birds, beasts, humans, and livestock—wherein lies discrimination? After a long silence, he said: "If you are not a guest from Dragon Gate..."
Be careful not to suffer a "marked forehead" (a public humiliation).
When the Buddha ascended the hall for his *nirvāṇa*, he spent his life merely dragging out empty proclamations; in the end, he could not even maintain himself.

Whether he entered *parinirvāṇa* or did not, neither was truly my disciple. He turned this worn-out sack inside out until it was completely emptied; in the blue heavens, one more grievance has been added.
How bitter! To turn gold into dung and soil—how regrettable!
Ascending the hall, he said: "Do not seek it in the Buddha; do not seek it in the Dharma; do not seek it in the Sangha. The spring flowers are in full bloom;
the spring affairs are intricate and entangling. If you try to understand this through the 'spring mood,' you will only needlessly provoke spring sorrow."
Ascending the hall for the Bathing of the Buddha ceremony: Today, Siddhārtha emerges from his mother’s womb; unexpectedly, the world before his eyes is filled with dust.
This mountain monk pours forth the waters of West Lake, and with a straightforward heart, washes him from head to toe. Yet, he neither washes away the dust nor cleanses the body.
In the end, what is there to wash? Descend from the seat. Together we shall go to the hall to reveal the truth to everyone. Regarding the commencement of the summer retreat:

on the fifteenth day of the fourth month, we shall begin together; here in this land and in the Western Heaven (India) there is no difference. We shall spend the entire period of *an-guo* (the summer retreat) in diligent practice.
One can only obtain a single peg. Willow catkins are not the snow from the edge of the sky.
Entering the hall: To affirm a phrase is to erase it; to deny a phrase is also to erase it. The public case is already established; there is no need to clear it away or distinguish it.
Blind donkeys chase one another’s tail as they pass over to Silla. Linji and Deshan merely blink their eyes in vain.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The eye is like a shooting star; the faculty is like a flash of lightning. Having passed through the gate of the South Mountain, one has not yet seen the face of the South Mountain.
Is there anyone who wishes to see the bottom of the South Mountain? The weather is somewhat hot; let us meet again at another time."
Ascending the hall for the concluding distribution of offerings during the celebration of the Empress’s birthday: The Buddha-mother Māyā manifested in the body of a sovereign lady;

she withdrew into the profound mystery and attained tranquility through the One. Noble beyond compare, her wealth is peerless. As this festival of her long life arrives, the four seas resound with joy.
May we take the true news of the Western Patriarch and look up to pray for the Emperor’s reign to flourish for ten thousand myriad springs.
Ascending the hall: One is not accomplished; two is not right. To establish [a position] deviates from the source; to sweep away [all views] misses the essential intent.
Suddenly, if there were a monk who came forth and said, "Neither is it like this," even if the staff of Nanshan were broken, I would still not let you go for thirty years.
Suddenly, there was a flash of realization. He ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddha-dharma is not separate from daily life; in daily life, one hits the mark every hundred times. Yet for the patch-robed monks, when the string is plucked, they distinguish the melody;
when the leaves fall, they know the autumn. Why is it that out of ten, five pairs are found? When questioned, their mouths are like flat eaves. People—
The poor have short intelligence; when a horse is thin, its hair is long.

Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat, a monk asked, "Fengxue rewarded the labor of the nine-month summer retreat; we request that you, Master, provide words of recommendation.

Fengxue said, "A handful of fragrant grass has not yet been grasped, and the six-ringed golden staff resounds, shaking the void. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "The life-bloodline is interconnected."
"The arrow-points meet"—this is not without the Elder Fengxue; yet if one examines it closely, he cannot avoid the fault that small kindness obstructs great kindness.
Nanshan is not like this: if someone were to ask, "The summer retreat is over and the labor has been rewarded;
please, Master, offer a recommendation," he would take up his staff and strike him immediately. Why? Because from the beginning, Nanshan has never dared to fail the monks.

On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall for instruction. He cited Panshan’s saying: "The mind-moon is solitary and perfect; its light swallows the myriad phenomena. The light does not illuminate objects, nor do objects exist.
When both light and objects have vanished, what is this thing? The Master commented: "How great indeed was Panshan!"
He sat beneath Black Mountain. South Mountain was not so; there, light and object both vanish, leaving one free to take south for north.
Entering the hall, he said: "As for the two words 'Buddha-dharma,' I do not fear their being worn away. A swift and clever monk sees the corner through a wall;
Linji and Deshan missed this one move."
Ascending the hall: When skill is exhausted, simplicity emerges; when the water arrives, the channel is formed. Every step taken and every foot placed—crosswise and lengthwise, in all directions.
Even three thousand miles away, Nan-shan has already changed your eyes for you. If you do not believe this, try to feel for it with your hands and see.
Ascending the hall: Xuefeng rolls the ball; Heshan beats the drum. If you seek their ultimate intent, the moon does not break through the five [phases]. Ascending the hall:
It cannot be grasped, it cannot be relinquished, it cannot be described. The blue-eyed barbarian of the Western Heaven exhausts all his strength yet does not recognize it.
Whether recognized or not, Linji and Deshan are rebels in a time of peace.
Ascending the hall: To cease mental activity while remaining mired in the source is for the bright faculty to be naturally obscured. Where the Patriarch knew there was, you all do not know;

where you all know there is, the Patriarch does not understand. Whether one knows or does not know, whether one understands or does not understand—under the laws of the land, there are three thousand articles of offense.
Ascending the hall: Since the time of the Patriarchs, there has been nothing but mutual deception; in groups of two or three, they scratch an itch through a boot.
This mountain monk has never opened his mouth, yet already the hair of a tortoise grows many fathoms long.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the 'Single Tune of Yunmen'? Yunmen said, "The twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. The Master said:
"When one sees through to the bottom and employs it with intimacy, the *yangchun* melody is no longer the same tune; entering the water, one beholds the tall man."
A pity that gold is treated like excrement and soil; it is scattered upon the people of Jambudvīpa with no regard for them. Venerable Vinaya Master, ascending the hall:
You who have filled the monastic groves, you of immeasurable capacity! You stand at the forefront of the Dharma-battle; your pure mechanism is experienced in every palm.
Even if the thousand Buddhas were to appear, you would still strike one decisive blow. Why? Because under the Southern Mountain Gate, the command is carried out with singular authority.

[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "Deep hearing leads to shallow realization; shallow hearing leads to deep realization. People only know how to hasten their progress, unaware that they have missed the path.
Is there anyone who does not miss the path? Recognize the very first step."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The entire earth is scorching stones and melting gold; everyone says it is hot.
Only the staff of the South Mountain Master—its three hundred and sixty joints and eighty-four thousand pores—is shivering with cold.
Can you all believe this? If you cannot believe it, thirty years from now you will nod your heads in the dark. Do not say it was not the mountain monk who spoke."
Much talk. Ascending the hall:
Heaven has no gate; earth has no door. Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti have let go of their hands and departed.
If a patch-robed monk can insert his beak here, I shall divide the Southern Mountain monastery in half and give it to you to dwell in.
Ascending the hall: Deep, firm, profound, and remote; no one can reach it. Before the mountain lies a patch of idle field, where pines and bamboos face a vast, surging breeze.
The old barbarian with the missing teeth did not attain the wondrous truth.
Ascending the hall: For nine years he sat in a daze; the barbarian monk had no wondrous secret. The road to Chang’an is level and smooth; travelers at night never cease.
Ascending the hall for the summer retreat: The mouth of the hemp sack is tied; the path of sage and ordinary is cut off. A wax man in ice; a goose guarding the snow. Western Heaven.
"So it is. Is this land any different? Tell me, where is the difference? Today, Nanshan bit his own tongue.
[He] ascended the hall and cited Deshan’s address to the assembly, which said: "To ask is to have a fault; not to ask is likewise deviant.
At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. Deshan struck him immediately. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question; why did you strike me? Deshan said: [The text ends here.]
"Wait for you to open your mouth; what can you possibly do? The Master picked up the case and said: "How could this great Deshan have such a 'dragon's head and snake's tail'?
At that time, when the monk said, 'I haven't even asked a question yet; why are you hitting me?
he should have immediately stripped off his patched robe and given him a severe beating. Had he been a true man, he would surely have had a different way of life."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The silk thread at the tip of the fishing pole does not disturb the waves; the mechanism beyond measure—how could it follow the beaten track?
As for Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout, tell me: are they the silk thread at the tip of the pole, or are they the mechanism beyond measure?
If one cannot find flowing water, one must surely pass over other mountains."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Right here! Right here! A man of immeasurable capacity cannot even lift his feet.
How pitiable—this dead Zen monk, still prattling on with his lips hanging from his teeth. Nanshan simply whispered into his ear:"
Xuan Sha said, "The foundation of the teaching.

He ascended the hall and said: "The administrative framework of the Buddhas of the past; the very lifeblood of the Buddhas of the future. For a patch-robed monk, this is like an ancient calendar hanging at the waist—surely every three years there is one intercalary month.
Even though it is thus, I do not know how breaking the mirror at Dongping compares to striking [the wall] at Lingyun."
He broke the mirror. After a long silence, he said, "Study!
He ascended the hall and said, "Gold is tested by stone; jade is tested by fire. But tell me, by what do you monks test [the truth]?
After a long silence, he said, "Defeated! Defeated!"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "If you wish to see what is before you, do not harbor notions of compliance or resistance. Even when the Patriarch spoke thus, it still exhausted his teeth and jaws.
Nanshan is not like this: compliance is simply compliance; resistance is simply resistance. Blasted by the sun and buffeted by the wind, it is but a single piece of stubborn rock."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The water-buffalo of the east and west streams; the imperial transformation throughout the four seas and five lakes.
The Zen of the finger-pointing of Jizhi is inexhaustible for a lifetime of enjoyment. Zhaozhou’s lack of discrimination could not be fully elucidated for five years.
Nanshan could no longer restrain his impatience. He struck the meditation staff once and said: "Today, a light reward is given for a heavy price."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked an old master, "When the myriad realms come to invade, what should one do? The master replied, "Do not concern yourself with them.
The Master commented: "How busy that great old master already was! If someone were to ask me at Nanshan, 'When the myriad realms come to invade, what should one do?
I would simply say to him: 'What do you call the myriad realms? Even so, if there is no one to raise [the question]..."
The strength to uproot mountains with a tripod; a thousand-li black steed is not easily ridden.
Entering the hall, a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs?
Yunmen said, "A steamed bun. The Master said, "Do you all recognize Yunmen? Fat and clumsy, yet without a belly hole; illiterate, yet possessing the means to spend."
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "Even if the mind were to penetrate infinite time, throughout kalpas it has never been different from today.
But tell me, what is the matter of today like? The Indian wax man is as cold as ice; the monk of this land has not yet nodded his head."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "The Patriarch taught: 'There is no need to seek the Truth; one must only cease false views.

If you can cease them, the pure and wondrous lands of all Buddhas are within the eyebrows and eyelashes of each of you. If you do not cease them, you may as well go on crashing through walls and bumping into pillars."

Ascending the hall, the Master raised up an instance where Zifu addressed the assembly, saying: "If one sees the pagoda of Zifu from across the river and turns back immediately, I would give them thirty blows right under their heels;
how much more so for those who actually cross the river! As soon as a monk stepped forward, Zifu shouted, "Unfit for conversation!
The Master commented: "Although this old fellow Zifu exerted his full strength in his guidance, how could he..."
In that which has no path, one instead creates a path. As for Nanshan’s point of view, how is it? “The mouth of the alms bowl faces the sky. Entering the hall, he said:
“True emptiness does not obstruct existence; true emptiness is not different from form. He picked up his whisk and said: “Tell me, is this...”
Existence is not existence; form is not form. If you are a clever monk, you should seize the moment to transform into a leopard;
if you hesitate, you will have your nostrils pierced by the whisk.
Ascending the hall: More than half of the summer retreat has passed. Those who have long practiced may become complacent; yet a sharp-witted monk severs it all with a single bite.
But tell me, what is it like after it is severed? "When one has a mouth, it is fit only for eating."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "Who can obtain the Buddha-dharma of Huangmei? The Patriarch replied, "One who understands the Buddha-dharma obtains it.
The monk asked, "Can you, Master, obtain it? The Patriarch said, "I do not obtain it. The monk asked, "Why not?"
The Patriarch said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. The Master commented: "Murder may be forgiven, but rudeness is difficult to tolerate.
He ascended the hall and said, "The two words 'Buddha-dharma' stir up waves upon level ground. To wash one's feet and then board the boat already violates the meaning of things.
He struck his staff once and said, "Be careful not to let the prisoner remain, lest it foster further delusion."
Ascending the hall, he cited the case of Changqing entering the hall. Once the assembly had gathered and settled, Changqing dragged out a monk and said, "The assembly, prostrate to this monk!
He then asked, "Tell me, what excellence does this monk possess that you have ordered the assembly to prostrate?"
The assembly was speechless. The Master picked up the matter and said, "When I have explained it clearly to you, you still do not understand; how much less can you cover it over?
Changqing’s labor was in vain, and he could not avoid being ridiculed by those looking on."
At Xie Meishan, the Master ascended the hall for the West Hall ceremony. He raised the case of Changqing Heshang, who said:

"When one meets a fellow traveler on the path and passes by with shoulders touching, the work of a lifetime of study is finished. The Master commented: "Changqing speaking thus leaves his fellow travelers no small amount of frustration.
But as for this fellow traveler coming to touch shoulders—does he still have the matter of study to attend to? Unless one knows the heart [of the matter], one will not understand."
In vain do we speak of the cold of winter.
[The Master] ascends the hall and says: "I do not sit in the Palace of the Empty King; I do not don the robe of original nature. What need is there to act thus?
One must strictly avoid the time before birth. Do you all see the ancients? The whole family has sent them off on a boat at the river's edge.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised up the words of Fayan: "When the three rounds of the drum have ceased, they all come crowding forward;
the Buddha-dharma and human affairs are both completed at once. The Master commented: "Big and small Fayan are washing mud in the mud. Nanshan said:
"When the three rounds of the drum have ceased, they all come crowding forward; how much of their majestic radiance do you all diminish! Nanshan would sink three feet into the earth."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The first phrase is nothing more than direct bestowal. Nanshan has a mouth, yet he dares not speak erroneously. Why?
It would cause the pillar to burst into laughter."
Ascending the hall: In the school of the Patriarchs, a span of water can produce waves a hundred feet high.
If you can see through this, the jewel in the topknot of a Wheel-Turning King is not worth a single coin. If you cannot see through it, Kāśyapa’s rag-robe is more precious than the entire Sahā world.
Thousands upon thousands of dead Zen monks—what can Linji and Deshan do for them?

Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat: Restraining the feet to protect living beings—throughout India and this land, these are all gates of death; they are ultimately not the path of life.
Suddenly, there might be a monk who does not truly understand the matter who comes forward and says, "I do not even restrain my feet."
To be born is not to be protected against. Boiling *huanglian* with its roots—this is not yet bitter.
Entering the hall: The Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past have been blowing dust against the wind; the descendants of later generations wander lost in the midday sun.
Yet one remembers the old, ancient adept He Shan, who, whenever he met someone, would invariably say, "I know how to beat the drum."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "When Gaoting saw Deshan, Deshan beckoned to him from across the river; Gaoting strode straight across. The Master addressed the assembly, saying:
'Although Gaoting displayed his brilliance for a moment, he still remained separated from Deshan by the river.
Upon the Qiantang River, monks come and go like a weaving shuttle, yet this mountain monk has never beckoned anyone. Is there anyone here who would stride straight across?'"
“Did you cross over? After a long silence, he said, “Who would believe you?
Ascending the hall, he said: “Buying high in the east and selling low in the west—this is the secure and stable field of the monk, where one may play with ease and freedom.
But if you come to the gate of our Southern Mountain, there is another aperture: once you have been examined, you shall be struck.”

Ascending the hall, he said: "If you open your mouth, you cannot hit the mark; yet it is by chance that a composition is formed. If you open your mouth and do hit the mark, you are still separated by an ocean.
Carrying their bags and bearing their bowls, two by two and three by three—let us set aside the cost of the gruel and water for now; who will repay the price of the straw sandals?"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "A direct and decisive phrase—no one can bring it forth. The Seven and Forty, the Twenty and Three—all the old monks of the world—are merely gazing at the clouds or climbing trees.
When it comes to this point, what shall we say of Nan-shan? The mid-winter cold is severe;
each of you should return for now to a warm place."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "You sons of the Buddha, do not engage in false imaginings! A cow in Huai Prefecture eats grain; a horse in Yi Prefecture suffers from a bloated belly.

Even if Nan Shan were riddled with holes for you to pass through, it would still not exempt you from the heavy staff in my hand. Why is this? Once you have passed through the Dragon Gate, the wind and waves become even more perilous."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] related: "When Yunmen arrived at Qianfeng, he said, 'I ask the Master to answer my question. Qianfeng said, 'Have you even reached the old monk yet?
Yunmen said, 'Is that so? Is that so? Qianfeng said, 'I thought monkeys were white; it turns out there are also black ones. The Master commented:
"Meeting face-to-face, there is no need for anger; you are destitute, and I am poor as well. Thinking one has already risen early, one finds there is still night."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "Seven stars of the Southern Dipper, eight stars of the Northern Dipper. When the wind comes, the trees move; when the fish swim, the water becomes turbid.
You all, thirty years from now, will have your eyes opened. Do not say that Nanshan has a mouth but no tongue."

Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: For ninety days of *an-guo* (sitting in seclusion), the entire earth is devoid of paths for travel. The mind does not dwell upon the profound; the eyes do not hang upon the door.
The mouth of the sack is opened, and heaven and earth are revealed alone. Ten thousand *li* are without a blade of grass; treading upon it is unlike anything else.
When Master Biepu arrived, he ascended the hall. "To fully uphold that which transcends [the ordinary] still involves traversing a journey.
Holding his staff horizontally, he said, "The Great Function manifests before us; no fixed rules remain. "Nanshan," he said, "today the Great Function departs!
Everyone, take care of your own eyes and nostrils! Leaning on his staff, he said, "Enough, enough! Before those with clear eyes..."
Ascending the hall: pushed forward, he does not advance; pulled back, he does not retreat. Linji’s “white-handed” theft was not yet a masterful hand.
Nanshan does not begrudge his two eyebrows; his jade-like whiskers are vainly used to prop open a tiger’s maw.

Ascending the hall: I have always been earnest about this; the hidden intent lies with you. The qilin and dragon do not serve as auspicious omens; the crane and tortoise naturally become immortals. Ascending the hall:
Where the Buddhas and patriarchs have not reached, take one step. Where the Buddhas and patriarchs have not spoken, utter one word.
Tell me, why did Deshan set up his signboard in the bustling marketplace? The people of Yin used cypress; the people of Zhou used chestnut. Entering the hall:
East, west, south, north—everywhere one stumbles and strikes against things. In the four quarters and above and below, the heavens are level and the earth is level.
The Buddha-dharma is truly vast and great, yet there is no one to testify to it. *Duh!* I am walking through the wild weeds, while you have entered a deep village.
Ascending the hall, he suddenly took up his staff, called out to the assembly, and said:
"The hundred thousand Dharma gates and immeasurable subtle meanings—the staff itself shall express them all in a single phrase for you. He then struck the ground with it once and said:
"If you look further behind or ahead of this, the mountain monk will incur immeasurable transgression."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The tall have the Dharma-body of the tall; the short have the Dharma-body of the short.
