'Striking the collar from the sleeve, or cutting the lapel from under the arm'—I do not ask about that now. You people, a signboard has been set up at the gate of Zihu; tell me, what matter does it clarify?"
Ascending the hall: The staff and the shout clash like a flash of thunder; wild words and inverted speech issue from a tongue three inches long.
From the southern region one strikes all the way to the head of the northern region—how could the turtle ever have been lost within the jar?
Incense is burned on the anniversary of Pō’ān’s death. A foster son cannot equal his father; the family lineage will decline for a generation.
Crossing mountains to seek the tracks of ants—how many people could possibly know? He then burns incense, saying: "Old Monk, you know and I know.
Do not let this celestial secret be leaked."
Ascending the hall: The Dharma before one’s eyes is encompassed right before one’s eyes. The Brahmin who sat facing a wall for nine years could not see through it.
If he had been able to see through it, the horse from Haidan would have been as large as a donkey.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Those who know it cannot speak; those who cannot speak, however, do know it.
If one point is not penetrated, both points lose their efficacy. He suddenly took up his staff and said, "Nanshan, today I shall treat this as a dead horse.
He struck the ground once and said, "Half is saved."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The eternal void of ten thousand ages; the wind and moon of a single day. Ānanda, you have been constantly selling 'qiao' [a type of wine] in the fish markets and taverns.
Why is it that the Bodhisattva Without Supernatural Powers is so difficult to find his traces? After a long silence, he said:
"When two people share the same heart, their bond is stronger than gold."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Even for one who is non-active and without affairs, there remains the difficulty of the golden chain.

You all, throughout the twelve periods of the day—walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—how can you avoid this fault? After a long silence, he said: "On Mount Song there is a man named Pò-zào-duò."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Xuefeng, who said: "The entire earth is the gate of liberation; yet, taking him by the hand, he refuses to enter.
The Master commented: "Old man Xuefeng, why such a desperate hurry? I dwell in a monastery on the South Mountain;
with a hundred affairs tormenting me, what leisure do I have to drag you into the gate of liberation? Nevertheless, one must recognize gratitude."
Few are those who repay kindness; many are those who harbor resentment.
Entering the hall, he raised an ancient case: A monk asked Yantou, "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Yantou said, "Who is it that arises and ceases?"
The Master held up the case and said: "Cold water is poured into a boiling cauldron; the tongue does not leave the mouth.
What a pity that old Yantou—his compassion has become a fault.
He then ascended the hall and, citing a monk’s question, said: "A monk asked Shishuang, 'What is the phrase transmitted outside the teachings? Shishuang replied, 'Not a phrase.'"
Yunmen said, "A non-phrase is precisely a phrase. The Master commented: "One coffin, two corpses.
He ascended the hall and cited a monk’s question to Yantou: "What is it like when one encounters a fierce tiger on the road? Yantou said, "Press forward! The Master commented: "How great was Yantou!
He frightened him so that he forgot what came before and lost track of what followed."
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: An ancient said, "If you wish to recognize the ever-abiding, non-fading nature, recognize it in the midst of the transformation and change of all things.

Now, when the mass of yin has been stripped away and the single yang returns—this being precisely the time of the transformation and change of all things—where, after all, does this ever-abiding, non-fading nature reside?
One winter, two winters... [the master] folds his hands across his chest.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Baofu, "Throughout his life, what words or phrases did Xuefeng have that allowed him to reach the state where 'the wild sheep hangs from a horn'?
Baofu replied, "I cannot fail to be a disciple of Xuefeng.
Xuedou commented, "Of the fifteen hundred monks, Baofu was the one who stood out. The Master commented: "How great is Xuedou! Like...
When people eat plums, they bite only at the red edge. Nanshan is not like this: "Raising a son who does not equal his father brings a generation of decline to the family line.
He ascended the hall and cited Nanquan’s address to the assembly: "Last night, Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra gave rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma, and were banished."
Facing the two Iron Ring Mountains, the Master picked up the staff and said: "The order has been fully executed; even Nanquan cannot be blamed for this.
Here at Nanshan, if anyone gives rise to views of Buddha or views of Dharma, I invite them to drink a bowl of tea.
Now tell me, why does Nanshan go against the ancients? 'When meeting, one does not dismount from the horse; each goes their own way toward the future.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Linji’s Three Mysteries and Three Essentials; Dongshan’s Five Ranks of Ruler and Subject; Fenyang’s Ten Wisdoms of Shared Reality; Huanglong’s Three Barriers;
the hundred thousand miles east and west, the eight thousand li north and south—coming and going everywhere is not as good as being right here."
Nanshan: Today we borrow water and offer flowers. Everyone must take care not to mistake the bell for a jar. Entering the hall:
Master Balingsheng had three turning words throughout his life to repay Yunmen. He never performed memorial services during his lifetime.
Yesterday was the anniversary of the late Master’s passing; Nanshan has prepared this meager offering as a small tribute. There is also one...
A turning word. Do you all remember it? If you do remember it, the Old Barbarian has hope for you.
If you do not remember it, he suddenly picks up his staff and says: "Staff, let me help you from beginning to end. He strikes once.
The heavens are high—who listens by their side? The earth is vast—few are those who understand.
Entering the hall: Autumn winds wither the fallen leaves; the traveler has not yet returned home. Even if one were to return, there would be no place to establish a livelihood.
White artemisia and red smartweed face the reeds; they cause one to long remember Old Xuansha.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Xuansha, “The entire earth is a single bright pearl; why is it that this student cannot comprehend it?
Xuansha replied, “What need is there to comprehend it? The Master commented: “How great is Xuansha! He has, however, offered up a confession of death right in this monk’s hands.
If it were Nanshan, he would wait until the monk had asked, ‘The entire earth is a single bright pearl,’ and then [respond]...”
Why does the student not understand? I simply say to him: "Go! Who will believe you? This is to leave him in a state of total embarrassment.
Ascending the hall: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. When the tree falls, the vine withers. One must strictly avoid planting roots here.
Arrayed clouds stretch across the sea; drawing the sword, one stirs the dragon’s gate."
Xin Dacheng ascends the hall to accept an invitation. He cites the words of Xinghua: "Whenever I meet a person, I come forth; yet when I come forth, it is not for the sake of others.
He then cites the words of Sansheng: "Whenever I meet a person, I do not come forth; yet when I do come forth, I am immediately acting for others. The Master comments:
"These two great elders met and did not dismount from their horses; each simply galloped on toward his own future path. Xin Dacheng, however, will never tread upon the tracks of the ancients."
Footprints: there must naturally be a path by which they emerged. Descend from the seat.

When the administrative heads and chief officers join in invitation for the Buddha-bath ceremony and ascend the hall, pointing to heaven and pointing to earth—what "handle" are you seeking? Nailing it down and gluing it shut; scraping with knives and washing with water.
"A ladle of fragrant soup for one's descendants is much like being respectful yet lacking in propriety.
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat, he struck the empty air with a *baobao* sound; the stone man and the wooden man both responded in unison.
"In the sixth month, snow falls in profusion. This is the Great Perfect Enlightenment of the Tathāgata. The Master said: "The ancients once acted in this manner..."
How do you say it? "White jade is flawless, yet it has a flaw; the pleasures of the road never reach home.
Now tell me, what is the phrase for reaching home? Wait until the ninety days are finished, and then I shall present it to you all.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Śākyamuni has already passed away; Maitreya is not yet born. It is precisely this world without a Buddha, where the great earth collectively enjoys peace and prosperity.
He struck his staff once and said: "I do not intend to strike the grass; I simply wish to startle the snake."
Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the summer retreat, the Master raised an old case: A monk asked Fengxue, "Today marks the end of the summer retreat; what is your intention, Master?

Fengxue replied, "A handful of fragrant grass has not yet been plucked; the six-ringed golden staff rings out, shaking the void. The Master commented, "How grand, Fengxue! Yet he is still floating and constrained.
Suppose someone were to ask me today, at the end of the summer retreat at Nanshan, 'What is your intention, Master? I would simply say:"
He said to him: "Let us set aside the cost of ninety days' worth of rice for now; who will repay the cost of the gruel and water?
If one possesses the 'three-cornered eyes,' a patch-robed monk can immediately transform like a leopard seizing the moment."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wondrous intent is swift; words and explanations arrive late. A guest of honor at the Dragon Gate knows before it is even raised.
But tell me, what is this matter that is known? The Lady of the Moon does not paint her brows."
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: The nine-month summer retreat is finished; the knot on the sackcloth bag is untied.

For the patch-robed monk, there is no fixed destination—whether it be Mount Heng or Mount Tiantai. Only when you stumble midway and strike your toes will you realize that this single summer at Nanshan has not been in vain for you.
The posthumous letter from Master Miaofeng of Lingyin arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The great road that penetrates heaven is ten thousand layers of iron walls.
When one pierces through with the full power of one's being, one laughs the void to pieces. When the wild sheep hang their horns, no trace remains."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Ordinarily, I speak upside-down and backwards; when have I ever opened my mouth or moved my tongue?
This does not hinder adding frost to snow, so let me settle this matter once and for all with you all. Holding up his whisk, he said: "Tell me, what is it?"
Recorded Sayings of Venerable Shitán, Volume One;
Recorded Sayings of Venerable Shitán, Volume Two;
Recorded Sayings from Jingde Lingyin Chan Monastery in the Prefecture of Lin’an.
The Dharma-heirs, Liaojue and Shitan and others, compiled [this record] and entered it into the temple.
Pointing to the triple gate, he said: "The gateless gate—open in seven ways and accessible in eight. The single word 'enter' is not even necessary.
He let out a shout and then departed.
He held up the imperial edict: yellow paper with black characters, impossible for the eyes of the multitude to deceive. Yet, there is one character within it that is cryptic;
the visual power of everyone fails to reach it. Tell me, which character is it? This mountain monk does not wish to point it out myself, so I instead ask the Rector to explain it.

Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "There is a path to be traveled; it rises higher and higher to Mount Sumeru, the King of Lamps. Withdrawing his body and joining his palms, he then ascended the seat with rapid strides.
Having offered incense and made prayers for the Emperor, he adjusted his robes and took his place. Addressing the assembly, he said: 'Every dharma is the original dharma;
there is neither dharma nor non-dharma. The Flying Peak is high, and the eye is likewise high; the Cold Spring water is azure, and the eye is likewise azure.'"
It is also azure. The cypresses, pines, bamboos, and cedars; the waterfowl and the forest groves—each abides in its own place, so that no man may find advantage therein.
Only I can know this for myself. If you understand it thus, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace are repaid all at once. If this is not yet the case, [do not be complacent].
"By chance, do not pass Hu-yuan Cave; hearing the sound of the monkeys, one fears it will break one's heart. (The words of thanks are not recorded. Again, [Master Dahui] raised the case:
When Baoshou was inaugurating his hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk. Baoshou struck him immediately.
Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher for others in such a manner will not only blind this monk’s eyes, but will also blind the people of the entire city of Zhenzhou. Baoshou then...
He returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master held up his whisk and said: "Baoshou and Sansheng—both were masters of their craft, yet both suffered a loss.
Although this monk was pushed out by others, he bought iron and obtained gold; what a display of wealth and honor!

Today, as I open the hall at the new Lingyin Monastery, there is no one to push a monk out either. I have simply made arrangements as the occasion required; when we meet, those who truly understand will naturally recognize us."
"Understood. Why must a pure breeze move heaven and earth?

That evening, during the small *sīmān* (private instruction), he spoke of mind and nature: "In shallow grass, it is easy for reeds to grow long. He cited the ancients and the present: "How can a bitter gourd serve as a guest?
Discerning the host within the guests—where the land is vast and people are few. Discerning the host within the host—one in ten thousand.
He gave a shout and said: "Host and guest are clearly distinct. Do you all believe this? If you can believe it, then when walking, I walk with you;
when sitting, I sit with you. If you cannot believe it, though we share the same boat and journey together, we are as far apart as Hu and Yue.
How can one speak a phrase that does not harm the meaning of things? After a long silence, he said: "It breaks through the azure..."
A thousand-foot pine falls; it cuts off the red dust of the world—a single stream of water. Again, he cites Xuan Sha’s address to the assembly:
“The teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the scriptures—since Bodhidharma came from the West, these must not be overlooked.
If they were not overlooked, they would not even suffice for a single shout. The Master comments: “Xuan Sha only knows how to step forward; he cannot avoid being laughed at by the bystanders.”
At New Lingyin, it is not so. Regarding the three vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, since Bodhidharma came from the West, he has let one point pass by.
Why? For fear of letting it rot.
Ascending the hall: "Eighteen, nineteen—the foolish person runs through the night. Nineteen, twenty—people do not believe it.
If they can believe it, there is Maitreya within the Hall of Avalokiteśvara."
Master Xie Jianshou ascended the hall. He raised the following case: A monk asked Xianglin, “What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
Xianglin replied, “In the eleventh month, fire burns the mountains. The Master commented: “In the eleventh month, the mountains burn; the flames blaze fiercely, enveloping all before one’s eyes.”
To borrow a hand to perform a fist-punch—if this were merely a matter for those beneath the patched robe—it would still fall short by one hundred and eight thousand leagues. Why?
Because one watches the hunt from the imperial palace; it is not the clearing of a thatched field.

On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall: "Heavy snow fills Chang'an; spring has come, yet it is especially cold. As for the Buddha-dharma at the start of the new year, not a single point is concealed.
But tell me: how many years old is the Stone Maiden of Huangmei? Speak quickly, speak quickly!"
The Abbot ascends the hall to thank the administrative staff: "Everyone knows there is this broken-legged cauldron;
with everyone lending a hand from left and right, we have spared the mountain monk all worry. Thus, I simply face south and gaze at the Big Dipper."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Qianfeng addressed the assembly, saying, "If you raise one, you must not raise two; to let pass one move is to fall into the second.
Yunmen came forth from the assembly and said, "Today someone has come from Tiantai and is going on to Jingshan."
Feng said, “The head cook shall not be required for general labor tomorrow. The Master took up the case and said: “Qianfeng wraps fine brocade around a stone;
Yunmen encases a lump of mud in iron. Wherever they strike or clash, their words are precise and their speech is upright.
Were it not for Ren Gongzi, one would toil in vain discussing fishing rods.”
Ascending the hall: I ask not of words, nor do I ask of wordlessness. The staff of Vulture Peak leans askew against the wall;
its splendor is fully possessed without spending a single coin.

Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, the retreat is entered; here in this land and in the Western Heaven, we travel the same path and tread the same tracks.
Yet, within this, there alone is the Ling Shan mountain—distinct, distinct, distinct! Hiding ice in the heat of the sun; fishing for turtles amidst the flames.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Zen of a single finger-tip of the ancients is inexhaustible for use throughout one's entire life.
It is so clear and so direct that it does not differ much from here at Vulture Peak. With a three-foot staff, I stir the Yellow River."

Ascending the hall: Day by day they change, month by month they transform; yet here we see them once more in the Middle Kingdom. As for this matter of the patch-robed monks—how can one even ask about it?
Everyone’s mouth falls silent. There is a paradox that cannot be borrowed from others: selling pine-wind in the sixth month; in the human world, it would surely be priceless.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "In the school of the Patriarchs, what 'nose' (essential point) is there to be sought? A spring breeze blows vast and boundless to the ears.
The grasses, trees, and groves; the lanterns and the pillar—all have attained the highest degree through the emptiness of mind. Why, then, do you all come here to doze off?"
Incense Offering on the Anniversary of Pó’ān’s Death: “Bālíng’s three turns of speech leave this old monk at a loss; at Vulture Peak there was not half a word.
To repay the kindness of Pó’ān—since there was not half a word, tell me, with what will you repay it?
‘No eyes, no painted brows’—few people understand this meaning.”
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Old Man Bimācāra held up his trident and refused to put it down. Here at Vulture Peak, all is utterly bare and starkly clean;
there is nothing to grasp. Suddenly, if a monk were to come forth and say, 'I have seen through you,' I would take out a separate cauldron from Vulture Peak to cook fragrant offerings for him.
Why? Because he is a live sparrow in the mouth of a fierce tiger."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example: One day Langya ascended the hall. A monk stepped forward and drew a circle.
Langya took up his staff and struck him, saying, "Speak! Speak! The monk said, "I do not speak; I do not speak. Langya asked, "Why do you not speak? The monk said—
"The Buddhas of the three periods of time do not transcend this. Yaoyuan then struck him and drove him out, whereupon he addressed the assembly, saying:
"In the Vinaya, to point a finger at a bhikṣu constitutes a *pāyattika* offense. Today, this mountain monk enters hell as swiftly as a shot arrow."
The Master picked up the case and said: "It was not Langya; he was misled by this monk. Had it not been for this monk, Langya’s command would not have been carried out in vain.
At the end, he sold a riddle on the tip of his staff, yet further hid his body within a pillar. This will make those who kept silent at Vaiśālī laugh to death."
At the conclusion of the summer retreat, Cuiyan ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "For the entire summer, we brothers have spoken here and there;
look, are Cuiyan’s eyebrows still there? Baofu said, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive. Changqing said, "It has grown. Yunmen said, "The barrier. The Master commented:
"Water flows to what is damp; fire seeks what is dry. In Lin’an, paper is expensive; one indictment for all."

Having taken charge of the duties, he offered thanks to the former and current administrators and head officers, then ascended the hall. He raised an example: One day Xuefeng ascended the seat and called out to the assembly, saying, "Look!
Look at the one on the east! Look! Look at the one on the west! If you wish to understand, he took up his staff, threw it down, and said: [The sound of the staff striking the floor].
"Understand it right here! The Master picked up [the staff] and said: "Although Xuefeng cuts through iron and chops through nails, in the end he still injures his own edge and offends his hand.
Lingshan, today I cannot help but imitate him. Look at the one on the east; look at the one on the west.
This mountain monk has no time for it either. He took up his staff, threw it down, and said: "Just understand it directly!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Monks from the Five Lakes, coming from the south and coming from the north—have you ever encountered Minggong Xiù upon the sea?

Whether you have encountered him or not, if you have encountered him, there must be something to it. But tell me, what is that thing? If you can utter a single turning word, I shall arrange it for you beneath this bright window."
Ascending the hall, [Dongshan] raised an ancient case: A monk asked Master Mazu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Come closer. When the monk drew near, the Master gave him a slap and said, "Six ears do not share a secret.
Huanglong Nan commented: "The ancients still said that six ears do not share a secret; how much more so for those of today, three hundred or five hundred gathered together to deliberate!"
"A disaster! A disaster! The Master took up the case, saying: "It is easy to distinguish flour from snow, but difficult to discern soot within ink.
It is easy to see Master Ma; it is difficult to see Huanglong Nan. Suppose someone were to ask Lingyin today, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
I would say to him, 'Come closer. When he has come closer, I would then say, 'Go.'"
Why is this? White clouds may briefly depart from the green peaks, but the bright moon cannot be made to descend from the azure sky.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall and cites the Venerable Xuefeng: "The world is ten feet wide; the ancient mirror is ten feet wide."
Xuansha asked, "How wide is the brazier? Xuefeng replied, "As wide as an ancient mirror. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented:
"Xuefeng and Xuansha, father and son, in their spirited exchange, were much like washing dirt in mud. If one looks toward the school of Linji, they are far, far removed.
But tell me, how is it under Linji’s gate? After a long silence, he said: 'Look at the color of the fire.'"
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff, struck it once, and said: "The son inherits the father’s vocation; follow it and practice it.
Among those who are like shadows and echoes, even three thousand miles away, is there anyone who is truly liberated? Step back! Step back!
After so much rain without sun, it hinders me from drying my leather sandals."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Attendant Guang, who said to Xuansha: "If you, my uncle, can attain the Way of Chan, I shall forge an iron boat and sail away upon the sea.
Later, when Xuansha was presiding over a monastery, he sent someone to deliver a message to Attendant Guang, asking:
"Have you yet finished forging the iron boat? The Master commented: "A fierce tiger does not eat meat that has already been submitted; it is a pity that Xuansha ran right into [Guang’s trap]."
Master Guang’s attendant, while in his net, ascended the hall on the Winter Solstice.
The seasonal mandate allows no respite; the first line of the hexagram has turned toward Yang. The Way of the Buddhas grows long, while the Way of sentient beings wanes.
Holding up his staff, he said: "This staff stands solitary and distinct. Now tell me: does it follow the seasonal mandate, or does it not?"
The Command: After a long silence, he said, "Understood.
He ascended the hall and said: "When the Patriarch came from the West, he feigned deafness and dumbness; the old monks throughout the land were like those who raise dust against the wind.
Although the Buddha at Vulture Peak could have made two fists out of empty hands, he could not avoid being seen through by Flying Eagle Peak. Why? Because of Lake Tai."

Spanning three provinces, on the occasion of the Heavenly Foundation Festival, he ascends the hall. When the World-Honored One held up the flower, Kāśyapa smiled; thus the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye has flowed forth forever.

The Buddhas of antiquity and the Buddhas of today share the same mind and the same path. Wind follows the tiger; clouds follow the dragon. As the festival opens for the Heavenly Foundation, [the truth] is extended.
Benediction: May his longevity equal that of the two high peaks, North and South.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If one dharma is not penetrated, myriad conditions will only then be seen through. Holding up his staff, he said, "This here is the myriad conditions;
which one is the single dharma? He struck it once and said, "I have never given you the wrong commentary."
Resigning from his administrative duties, he ascended the hall and said: "An ancient worthy once said: 'Simply take rice and place it in the bowl of no-mind;
naturally there will be someone to support the broken-legged cauldron. This is much like a fool planting flowers in the air, hoping to harvest a round fruit. Ling Shan does not do so."
"If I sit, you must stand; to sit together or stand together is to be a blind man. Not a blind man—take hands and let us all walk over there.
He ascended the hall and said: "On the sea, Master Minggongxiu; Zhaozhou, East Hall and West Hall. Without shifting so much as a hair’s breadth, one ascends with level steps."
"Cloud-ladder. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, it is already the first or second grade. If you all understand it in such a way, you cannot avoid being seven or eight times mistaken.
It is the same as the stolen goods of a thief; it is not that there is nothing there.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying, "The entire earth is gathered up and made as small as a grain of millet;
it is tossed before you, yet you—lacquer buckets!—do not understand. Let us beat the drum and all go to look! The Master commented:

"Old man Xuefeng still has his teeth intact, and he brings trouble upon those who come after him. At Lingshan, it is otherwise: the entire earth is gathered up and made as small as a grain of millet."
He threw it before him. "A lacquer bucket will not do," he said. "Let us all go back to the hall for the communal work (fusshō).

Why? For fear of rotting that thing. He ascended the hall and said: "To study nothing and do nothing is to waste the offerings of the faithful. To run south and north is to betray one's own spirit. As soon as you see it fly by, turn back;
otherwise, the mud under your feet will be three feet deep. Now tell me, where does the mountain monk’s intention lie? Deep.
Shanwuwei’s Eyes.
Entering the hall, he raised the following case: Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Have you been here before? The monk said, "I have. Zhaozhou said, "Go and drink tea."
Furthermore, he saw a monk ask, "Have you been here before? The monk replied, "I have not. The Master said, "Go and drink tea.
The monastery director said, "If one who has been here is told to 'go and drink tea,' why is it that one who has not been here is also told to 'go and drink tea'?"
The State Governor summoned the head of the monastery. The master responded, "Yes. The Governor said, "Go drink some tea. The Master commented:

"This old fellow Zhaozhou has a heart like bitter ginseng and a mouth like honey; his single bowl of coarse tea is mostly empty and little substantial. The head of the monastery’s two eyes are squinting."
In the end, when have you ever actually eaten? Is there anyone who has truly eaten? You must urgently spit it out.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "When all of you open your mouths and speak, I am like one mute or speechless.
When I open my mouth and speak, you are like those intoxicated or dazed. Why is this? Barbarian words are easy to understand; Chinese speech is difficult to clarify."
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "It is not within; it is not without; it is not in between.
He struck the ground once with the staff and said, "In the morning one gazes upon drifting clouds; in the evening one listens to the murmuring stream."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou said, “The cypress tree in the courtyard.
The monk said, “Why do you, Master, point to an external object to show people? Zhaozhou said, “I have never pointed to an external object to show people.
The monk said, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou said, “The cypress tree in the courtyard.”
The Master held up the staff and said: "Straight as a string, curved as a hook; easy to see, difficult to recognize—this is old Zhaozhou at his wit's end.
Worldly affairs should be settled with justice; human hearts are hard to keep flowing like water."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Śākyamuni is stingy; Maitreya is wealthy. Licorice is sweet; yellow bitter-root is bitter. Phenomenon after phenomenon has little to do with one another;
each person must cross over for themselves. Tsk! Do not come to block the path to my ball court!"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Wuzu Fayan: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
'The cypress tree in the courtyard. To understand it in this way is already not so. What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
'The cypress tree in the courtyard. Only when you understand it in this way is it finally so. The Master commented: "Do you wish to see Wuzu Fayan? It is dark."
He pulled out the transverse bone from within and sat his tongue in the midst of clarity.
Entering the hall, he said: "Since the time of chaos thirty years ago, there has been no shortage of salt and sauce.
Master Mazu left a mess covering the ground. Ling Shan was not like this: since the time of chaos thirty years ago, there has been no shortage. After a long silence, he said: "The patched robe..."

"It is difficult for you to deceive me. He ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "Blind Chan practitioners realize through darkness; they lose their way in broad daylight. Those who hear deeply but awaken shallowly have not yet entered the true stream.
Is there anyone here whose entire capacity is liberated in solitude? He struck the staff once and said: "One does not reach the River Wu."
Unwilling to rest, he ascended the hall and said: "O Great Assembly! To ascend to heaven one does not rely on a ladder; throughout the earth there is no path to walk.
Alas, this shaven-headed monk from Duzhu studies the gait of Tang at Handan. Now tell me, how can one avoid this fault? Xuefeng rolls the ball; Yunmen draws [the bow].
Looking around, he ascended the hall and said: "A movement of the countenance reveals the ancient path; one does not fall into the trap of silent mechanisms. Those who rely on words perish;
those who linger in phrases are deluded. Not relying on words and not lingering in phrases—frogs leap up to the Brahma Heaven, and lanterns swallow up the pillar."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The superior person listens to the Dharma with the spirit; the middling person listens to the Dharma with the mind;
the inferior person listens to the Dharma with the ears. But tell me, with what does this staff listen? He struck the staff once and said:
"If one does not behold the falcon in the clouds, how can one know the cold of the desert sands?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Taking wide strides atop a hundred-foot pole; scattering true pearls within a purple silk curtain.
This mountain monk wins a hearty laugh—do you all understand? Speaking thus, tell me: is this a word of praise or a word of censure?
If you can determine this, the mountain monk and all of you shall share a single bowl of rice. If you cannot..."
He will certainly not emerge for thirty years. After that, someone will speak and break through [the barrier]. [The Master] ascends the hall:
"On the peak of Flying Eagle Peak, all is silent and empty of people; by the bridge over the confluence of streams, they gather in crowds and bands.
I do not ask about the *vajra-circle* or the *chestnut burr*; tell me, when your feet are planted firmly on the ground, bring forth a single phrase! After a long silence...
He said: "When asked a full sentence, he only spoke half a sentence.
He ascended the hall and said: "One phrase: a nail driven into wood. One phrase: wrapped right before one's eyes. One phrase: not used as a phrase.
He struck his staff once and said: "Were it not for Zhang Hua’s eye, one would vainly gaze at the light piercing the Dipper."
Ascending the hall at Xie Huqiu’s Double Sāla Trees: The true lineage of Dongshan has been as thin as a single thread;
the sleeping tiger has departed without a trace, yet now a single spot of its coat is seen once more. Though it is seen, tell me: how shall one communicate that phrase beyond the Sword Pond?
Kunlun puts on his iron trousers; with every step, he strikes a blow.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Movement is the sprout of the Dharma King; stillness is the root of the Dharma King. What do you call 'the Dharma King'?
A venomous snake swallows the turtle's nose; a filial son avoids his father’s name."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If one discusses this matter, why bother with many words? It is not within; it is not without;
it is not in between. After a long silence, he said: "Where Li Lou walks, the waves surge to the heavens."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Gautama originally possessed no supernatural powers; when did that old barbarian ever know they existed?

As for the monks beneath Lingyin who have reached a state of total completion and certainty—tell me, how do you intend to receive them? Thirty blows of the staff! For now, let us simply chop away the coarse."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you recognize the One, all matters are finished. Secret魔 (Bimi) brandishes his staff; Lu Zu faces the wall.
Even down to Linji’s Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, Dongshan’s Five Ranks of Sovereign and臣 (Minister), and Yunmen’s ‘Seventh’—you people, tell me:
is this it, or is it not? Last night, Old Lu of Xinzhou lost the jade stone from his waist."

Ascending the hall, he said: "I do not practice Chan; I do not discuss doctrine. Dragging along this tattered mat, I sleep in the daylight, deceiving these dead-end Chan practitioners who sit in cold indifference to this day.
At Vulture Peak, it was not so: while walking, one brushes aside the sleeves; by buying stone, one gains an abundance of clouds."
When the flowers are moved, the butterflies arrive.
Entering the hall, he roared like thunder and struck with staffs like rain. The great earth was devoid of even a speck of dust; turning one's head, there was nowhere to be found.
Nowhere to be found! Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan.
The Buddha ascends the hall for his final nirvana. For seventy-nine years, the great earth has suffered deception;

fortunately, the roots of this entanglement are severed today with a resounding crack. But tell me: what is it like after they are severed? The descendants of later generations will be as chaotic as three horses and nine disturbances.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If the Buddha comes, I strike; if the Patriarch comes, I strike. The old man Deshan truly displays his brilliance.
Here at Ling Shan, if the Buddha comes, I hit him; if the Patriarch comes, I hit him. As for the staff held in my hand, I shall set it aside for now. Why is this?"
Carrying tea and sweeping the floor—there must be one or half of one.
Entering the hall: the divine light is never obscured; it is a magnificent legacy for all ages. Once you have entered this gate, there is no room for intellectual understanding.
Qianfeng’s staff makes a single stroke; Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the thirty-third heaven. Why is it that ten [people]...?
There are five pairs. The eyes stare fixedly; fortunately there is no place where light does not reach, yet there is still a time when things are not clear.
[The Master] ascends the hall: "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns. Not knowing and not understanding, the matter is of one family.
Seeing much and hearing much, there are a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions. Ultimately, heaven has no second moon."

On the day of the Start of Spring, he ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying: "On the day of the Start of Spring, they beat the spring ox; the spring colors fill the forests and hills.
There is no doubt that it is beaten, but tell me, where does one begin? He struck the ground with his staff and said:
"Thirty years from now, do not say there is not much of a mess."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited Zen Master Longya, who said: "The sun rises over the connected mountains; the moon is full before the door. It is not that they have no bodies;
it is simply that they do not wish to reveal them in their entirety. [The Master] commented: "How great, indeed, is Longya! His tongue hangs outside his mouth. At Lingshan, however, it is not so."
Heaven has no gate; earth has no door. Everywhere one encounters him; his entire body is revealed alone.
Suddenly, if a monk comes forth and says, "I understand! I understand! you should simply say to him, "Du. Now, everyone, tell me: what is this character "Du"?
Ascending the hall: To seal the gate and silence the mouth already involves prolixity. All you elder monks of the world present your own bags of bewilderment;
I cannot help but let small kindness hinder great kindness. After all, how is it? A Persian merchant submerged in a crystal jar.

Ascending the hall: Last night I was so exhausted that I fell prostrate upon my bed; it was not until the fifth watch that I finally revived. Today, as I ascend the hall, I have no words or phrases to offer.
I simply ask the assembly to look upon me with understanding and not hold the wise against the foolish.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Stone of Dhūta is enveloped in moss; the Peak of Pen-thrown is entangled by *pi-li* vines.
One cannot add a single hair’s breadth, nor can one subtract a single hair’s breadth. At Luohan Monastery, three novices are ordained each year;
at Guizong Temple, one drinks tea after the formal session. Guizong is a worn-out old man: a flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech. Do you all understand?"
Do you understand? Afternoon meal bell tolls; Vajrapāṇi has turned pale.
Entering the hall: "Deshan is the vanguard; Linji is at the rear. Tell me, who is the one in between?
He plants his staff on the ground and says: "If your eyes flicker, you will be from East Lu or West Qin."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of the Fifth Patriarch Baizhang Yun, who addressed the assembly, saying:
"Baizhang does not know how to speak of Chan; the triple gate opens toward both sides. Sometimes when it is moved, the two bolts of the pivot—eastern and western panels—fly apart.
The Master said: "Lingshan does not know Chan; empty-handed, he clenches his two fists. The entire family is sent off on the road. I ask you all to continue the final line."

[Verse: The net is fine and the fish are dense; the medicine is abundant and the illness is grave. As the staff and shouts fly back and forth, there are those of the first and second grades. This mountain monk acts thus, flaunting his donkey-lips; the foolish guest needlessly exerts himself in exhorting the host. [Prose: Ascending the hall: When the net is fine, the fish are many; when the medicine is plentiful, the illness is severe. As the staff and shouts are exchanged in rapid succession, there are those of the first grade and those of the second.
This mountain monk displays his "donkey lips" in this manner—foolish guests labor in vain to advise their host.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "All sounds are the Buddha’s sound; all forms are the Buddha’s form. The goods are priced; the coins are full-value. This matter is for you all to deliberate upon:
how shall one discern and clarify that single phrase which turns the tongue upside down?
After a long silence, he said: "For those born under the Sheep, it is their natal year; for those born under the Tiger, it is a clash."
Ascending the hall: The spring light flows on; the spring days linger. The spring wind wraps around above, below, and in the four quarters.
The yellow oriole’s song comes from the west, amidst the willow shadows. To whom can this clear meaning be explained?
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you wish to see what lies before you, do not harbor thoughts of compliance or resistance. Wherever you strike or bump against it, there is nowhere to seek it out.
Hundreds of years ago, Yunju said, 'Why bother? Xinghua said, 'It is unnecessary. Does Ling Shan have anything to say as well?
When walking at night, do not step on white; it is not water—it must be stone."
Ascending the hall: Iron walls, iron walls, and yet again iron walls! There, there, and even further beyond!
When a matter reaches its ultimate limit, it must be decisively severed. A blind donkey leaps across the Western Heavens.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised up the case where Master Huayao Ying addressed the assembly, saying: "Seventeen, eighteen—turning a tortoise into a turtle.
Nineteen, twenty—people cannot believe it. One must further wait for withered wood to sprout flowers and for sesame cakes to yield juice. The Master said:
Although Lingyin is incapable, he must still meet with the flowers and medicinal herbs. On the seventeenth and eighteenth, he turns a tortoise into a turtle;
on the nineteenth and twentieth, he splashes ink at midnight. One must simply have withered wood sprout flowers and sesame cakes yield juice.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The public on the sea is brilliant and outstanding; yet the patch-robed monks do not know it exists. Suddenly meeting it in a cold place, one seeks it everywhere without success.
Seeking it everywhere without success—do not be careless! In the palaces of the Dragon King, who has ever arrived there in person?"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Upon this lump of red flesh, ten thousand fathoms stand sheer. The True Person of No Rank enters the realm of the three eyes and preaches the Dharma of liberation.
This mountain monk has been consistently lazy and indolent, passing the time just as it is. Do not mistake me for anything else;
only those of like path will understand."
Xie, the Head Seat and Chief Administrator, ascends the hall: "The marrow within Linji’s crown; the sinew within Yangqi’s eyes.
If you wish to clarify this matter, you must rely on this person. There is a path before the wind; the scale-tail has no stars.
Everyone wins, and all are joyful. But tell me, what is there to laugh at? I say it is because the scale-tail has no stars."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A blade does not cut itself; water does not wash itself. He took up his staff and said:

"The mountain monk’s staff has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up the heavens, the earth, and the great world. Where, then, can you all breathe out your resentment? He struck the ground once and said: "Kiai! (A clap).
Each returned to their original positions.
He ascended the hall and said: "The spring flowers are in full bloom; the spring light is about to fade. The cuckoo calls out again and again, escorting spring back home.
Why do you all not, at this very moment, attain clarity of vision and awakening of mind? When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, if there were suddenly someone among the assembly..."
The monk called out once. Shitō remained silent for a long while and then said, "I, this mountain monk, retreat three thousand paces.
He ascended the hall and said: "As clear as a mirror, as black as lacquer. The 'Four Sevens' and 'Two Threes' are mostly empty and little substantial. The staff of Vulture Peak—"
For now, I shall lean against the wall. Why? To avoid being subjected to the cold, critical gaze of bystanders.
Entering the hall: It is not that it is not; it is not that it is. To establish [a position] is to be eccentric; to sweep away [all positions] is to lose the essential meaning.
When Deshan and Linji come forth, they exchange what is within the skull.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised up the discourse: Panshan said, "The one path upward is slippery. Muzhou said, "Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high—perilous.

Linji said, "Like a spark from flint or a flash of lightning—it is dull. The Master said: "The eyes and nostrils of these three great elders are not the same, yet their hearts, livers, and five viscera are alike.
Although Ling Shan is incapable, this staff will exert its full strength for the sake of the assembly; indeed it does."
"A mere trifle. He struck his staff once and descended from the seat.
On the occasion of ascending the hall during the summer retreat, he said: "More than half of the ninety days have already passed. As for that matter, how is it ultimately?
Even if you exhaust it to the very bottom, in the end it still involves wind and waves. Suddenly, a monk came forward and said, "I know nothing at all. "A hundred... [The Master continued.]
It does not matter. When food comes, one opens the mouth; when sleep comes, one closes the eyes. To him, I simply say: "Go! Who would believe you, you wretched fellow?
The Record Secretary and Librarian [Xie] ascends the hall. He cites the Librarian asking a monk, "Why do you not read the scriptures? The monk replies, "I do not know."
The host said, "Why do you not ask someone else? The monk pressed forward with palms joined and asked, "What character is this?
The host was speechless. The Master said, "One who does not recognize characters yet recognizes them; one who ought to recognize characters yet does not recognize them.
Shitian makes such a judgment—tell me, where does his meaning lie? "Where ten thousand people look up in admiration, a single arrow brings down two eagles."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven; when a single speck of dust rises, the great earth is gathered up.
To go forth in this very manner is precisely to become a 'liberated white sand śrāmaṇera. Yet there is one person who does not yet consent. Why? Because Lake Dongting has no lid."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The green mountains do not lift a foot; beneath the setting sun, one does not pick up the lamp. Yellow-headed and blue-eyed, stinking meat attracts flies.
You people—if you attain realization after thirty years, do not blame this old monk."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old case: A monk asked Jingqing, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon reflected in water?

Jingqing said, "In the clear ripples, there is no path through. The monk said, "From where did you, Master, obtain this? Jingqing said, "If you ask again, from where would it come? The monk said, "At such a time as this, what is it?
Jingqing said, "Layer upon layer, mountain passes and roads. The Master said, "The Yellow-Faced One from Zhejiang has spent his effort..."

"What is the use of so many words? At that time, had he waited for this monk to ask whether the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in water, he would have simply said to him, "Layer upon layer, mountain passes and roads.
This would not only have cut off this monk's heels, but would also have opened the eyes of future generations.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The withered mulberry tree knows the wind from heaven; the seawater knows the cold of heaven. But tell me, what does the patch-robed monk know?
He knows that rice is made from grain. Even if you were to know this much, there will come a day when Old Yama demands the price for the meal."
Ascending the hall: The weather is cold and the days are short; when a drop of water falls, ice forms. The stone maiden of Huangmei sighs in silent lamentation upon the cold ground;
the Bodhisattva Anantagātra freezes his two ears to pieces. Do you all perceive this yet? If you do perceive it—
Matters are as one family. If you do not awaken, there is a place where you are stuck.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "In the kingdom of Magadha, there was no way for water to leak through; before the peak of Shaoshi, they came in threes and twos.
Reaching this point, without opening your mouth or moving your tongue, can you still bring it forth? He struck the meditation seat once and said: "And so..."
It cannot be gathered up or collected.
Entering the hall: Deshan’s raindrops of blows and Linji’s thundering shouts—when gathered together, they are scattered and fragmented.
Mount Ling: Clenching the teeth with determination, one can hardly lift it even with all one’s might. Why? Because Muzhou broke Yunmen’s leg. [He] ascended the hall: "At every moment it is midsummer;
every day it is the third autumn. In the midst of the bustling market, at the tips of the hundred blades of grass—there is the Old Man of Jia Shan."
Selling a steep cliff. A high price has not yet been met with a light recompense. Today, this mountain monk shall offer him a light price for it.
(He strikes his staff once. He calls out: "Old man Jiashan, in the end, one cash paid in hand is better than a thousand cash on credit."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "There is no dharma before one’s eyes; yet the intent lies right before one’s eyes.

From the Buddhas and Patriarchs of old down to all the elder monks in the world, their transgressions fill the heavens—day after day, day after day. Last night, while I was in my needle-case, I lost a single ancient coin."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wind does not come; the tree does not move. When the eastern house lights its lamp, the western house sits in darkness.
The dragon carries the ocean treasure, yet the fish swims on without a backward glance. Now tell me: is this the Buddha-dharma, or is it worldly truth?
If you all can discern between them, Shitian will give you a pair of straw sandals."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Westward Transmission has no intention; the Direct Pointing has no meaning. It has led all these foolish children to lie prostrate on the cold ground.
He struck his staff once and said, "Arise! I, this mountain monk, have a dose of 'sobering tea' for you. Some fellows will then say:
"What is the 'awakening decoction'? This was the ultimate teaching of Deshan. He ascended the hall and said:
"Much talk and many words have, from the beginning, led to mutual error. He took up his staff and said, "The staff of Vulture Peak has not led to error.
Do you all believe this? He struck the floor once with the staff and said, "How many people [are there]?"
Lost in the midday path. Ascending the hall.
On the first day of the month, ascending the hall. Having nothing to bestow as instruction, he simply dismissed them as they were. "You people may not necessarily be quick-witted;
you must rather wring out some essence from a weightstone, so that there may be a flavor to be had. After a long silence, he said:
If you see it and do not grasp it, it will follow you a thousand miles.
Entering the hall: Winding and twisting, level and smooth; pierced through in seven ways and eight holes, intersecting in ten directions.
You people may go east or west as you please, but for heaven’s sake, do not let yourselves bump into the lame old Yunmen!

Ascending the hall, he said: "To seize tigers and rhinoceroses, to distinguish dragons from snakes—eggplants, gourds, and rotten winter melons! This mountain monk has truly reached a point where there is no place to apply his hand.
After a long silence, he said: "Outside the gate, the Vajra-puruṣas sweat like rain."

Ascending the hall: When the meaning reaches and the phrase reaches, when the lineage is penetrated and the teaching is penetrated—whether it be the first chapter or the second, whether a hundred turns or a thousand layers—one must topple the mountain in front of one’s face.
Wearing a long robe and wide sleeves, one dances in the spring breeze. You impoverished ghosts, stop! Stop! Stop!
Furthermore, you must know there is the Bodhisattva Red-Crested King.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: Under the gate of Lingyin, there is an inviolable decree.

During these ninety days, from beginning to end, the path of the patch-robed monk has been kept alive; smoke rises from beneath his feet. This old monk will never, like Yunmen, demand payment for the rice he eats.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old case: A monk asked an ancient worthy, “How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day?
The ancient worthy replied, “A monkey eating a hair-worm. The Master commented: “Precisely when the mind is applied, precisely there is no application of mind.
A monkey eating a hair-worm—if you can continue this single phrase, then the work of study is finished.”
